title: Going offline wipes the loaded page while the banner says "Showing what was loaded"
what: When the connection drops after a page has loaded, Home, Timecards, Things to do, Time and Pay replace their content with "View paused" or an empty card. The shell banner says "You're offline. Showing what was loaded." at the same moment, and each page words the paused state differently.
why: Visibility of system status; the message contradicts the screen. A one-second Wi-Fi drop costs the whole view (Doherty).
fix: Pick one rule (see Decisions). Either keep body.content rendered read-only while phase is 'paused', with an amber "Offline · updated 9:24 PM" line and actions disabled, or keep the clearing and change the banner to "You're offline. Reconnect to see the latest." Use one paused message on every page.

decision.q: When the phone or computer goes offline, should pages keep what was already loaded, or clear it?
options: Keep the last loaded snapshot read-only, with an "Offline · updated 9:24 PM" line and actions disabled. Matches the banner and helps people on weak shop Wi-Fi.
Keep clearing for privacy (the X-Nevora-Failure contract) and change the banner to "You're offline. Reconnect to see the latest."
decision.rec: Keep the snapshot for a person's own shift, hours and lists, and clear only when the app is paused because the person stepped away. Either way, the banner must stop promising something the page doesn't do.

title: "Done and older" hides pending approvals
what: The page called "Done and older · Not counted in today's total" holds 18 timecards to approve, two time corrections waiting for review, 47 plan-ahead items and coverage gaps. An Owner or Manager who clears Things to do to zero still has 70+ open items.
why: The label promises finished work; pending payroll blockers sit behind it. Honest counts.
fix: Move Time corrections and Timecards to approve into Things to do as their own groups. Rename the entry "Later and done" with a count ("Waiting 22 · Done 4") and keep only decided items under Done.

title: White text and glass chips on the teal band fail contrast
what: Band sub-lines, live-figure labels, week-day letters, segment labels and search placeholders use 17 different white alphas and read at 3–4:1. Glass status chips ("Live", "Due", "Now", "Shift lead", "Tomorrow") measure 3.6–4.4:1, and the Clocker's "TIME CLOCK" label is 3.72:1.
why: WCAG 1.4.3: small text needs 4.5:1. This is the most-seen text on every main screen.
fix: Add two tokens: --b-on-band #FFFFFF for titles, figures and labels on glass, and --b-on-band-2 rgb(255 255 255 / .86) for sub-lines on solid band only. Delete the other 15 alphas. On the hero, use solid white chips with status ink (#8A4B00 amber, #1D6B45 green, #0B6E69 teal).

title: Phone tab-bar labels fail contrast on every page
what: The bottom tab labels are 10.5px grey #7D868B on a white bar, 3.71:1 (axe flags 3.68:1 on every phone capture). They are the primary navigation on every phone page for all four roles.
why: WCAG 1.4.3, at the smallest text size in the app.
fix: Set inactive labels to #6A7176 (4.96:1 on white) and keep the teal active state. Size stays 10.5px as approved.

title: The live-figure tiles are invalid list markup (axe "serious")
what:
Every Home live strip renders
. A link between the group and the term breaks the list, so screen readers lose the label and value pairing. axe flags it on 60 audits (368 nodes), for every role and at tablet width.
why: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and relationships (Level A).
fix:
Render the tiles as
  • labelvalue
. The link's aria-label already carries "Late: 0. Missed clock-ins".

title: The timecard backlog shows a different count on every screen
what: The same pending timecards read 11 on Home, "Approve 7 timecards first" on Time exports, "12 not finalized" in export options, 18 under Done and older and "Approved 0/12" on Timecards. One Timecards screen shows "Ready to approve 6" beside "Approve 3 ready", and "Attention 4" can't be traced to rows.
why: Honest figures: the Owner can't tell how much stands between them and payroll.
fix: Use one shared selector for "timecards to approve before payroll" on Home, Payroll, Time exports and Things to do, and name the scope on every count ("11 timecards from Nov 2–8"). Make the Attention tile filter the list and give each affected row an amber chip.

title: The Payday card hides overdue payroll and says "Ready now" for unreviewed work
what: Home shows next Friday's payday with an amber "In 11 days" chip while Payroll says two pay periods have no payroll and the Nov 6 payday has passed. Its three progress segments are unlabelled and never light, yet the line reads "11 timecards to review · Ready now".
why: The main screen says payroll is fine while paydays are missed. Honest status.
fix: When overdue periods exist, show the oldest with a red "Payday passed Nov 6" chip and "Prepare Oct 26 – Nov 1". Label the segments (Timecards, Review pay, Approve) or drop them, and replace "Ready now" with the state ("0 of 11 approved"). Hide the segments for roles without payroll.

title: Tap targets fall under the 48px rule on phones and tablets
what: Phone week arrows are 32–36px, sheet Save and Edit pills 36px, segments 34–36px, switches 51×31 and person checkboxes 20px. On touch tablets the rail is 40×48, top-bar controls 40px, back links 32px and schedule grid blocks 28px, because the desktop layer starts at 768px with no touch pass.
why: Fitts's law and DESIGN's "48px+ targets" (tablet mock: rail 48×48, top bar 44px). A few also miss WCAG 2.5.8.
fix: Extend the kit's ::after hit area (owner-b.css:84) to .b-week__arrow, .q-nav__r, .c-shift__save, .b-seg > *, .b-btn--glass and row buttons. Inside the tablet block add @media (pointer: coarse) with a 44px floor and 48×48 rail links. Make switch and checkbox rows the <label>. Use one row-action size (44px hit, 96px min width) and one footer-action size (48px).

title: A red "Needs an Owner" chip sits next to an active Fill button
what: Leave-repair rows carry a red "Needs an Owner" chip, yet the same row offers a teal Fill. The chip means "no one is assigned yet", which is neither a stop nor Owner-only.
why: Red means stop, so Managers read "you can't do this" while the button says the opposite.
fix: Change value "Needs an Owner", valueTone "red" to "Not assigned" in amber. If Managers truly can't fill these shifts, replace Fill with a grey "Ask an Owner".

title: Keyboard focus lands on invisible controls
what: While a page's access check runs, the "Refresh current view" button is clipped to 1px but stays focusable, so Tab lands on nothing. The Team search's visually hidden "Apply search" button is tabbable too, before the field.
why: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus visible and 2.4.3 Focus order.
fix: Render the refresh button only when stuck is true (or tabIndex={-1} and aria-hidden until then). Add tabIndex={-1} to both "Apply search" buttons; Enter in the field still submits.

title: Help can't be reached from the desktop sidebar or account menu
what: On desktop the sidebar's "More" is a group label, not a link, and the account menu holds only Profile, My pay and Sign out. Help, Scheduling rules and the More page appear only as back-link targets or in Ctrl K, which hides during access checks.
why: Recognition over recall; a help page people can't find doesn't help.
fix: Add Help to the account menu and as a sidebar footer link above "Powered by VELANI LLC". Point desktop back links at real parents, and reduce desktop More to My pay and Help or remove it.

title: Notifications failed to load on its default route
what: The plain Notifications route showed "Couldn't load notifications · Check your connection" at every width while online, as the bell claimed 3 unread. The message blames the connection; the logged deliberate error is a server 503.
why: An empty feature page and a wrong cause. Needs a check against the real route, not only the capture harness.
fix: Reproduce and fix the Owner notifications read so the bell and page agree. Say "Notifications didn't load. Try again." and mention the connection only when navigator.onLine is false. Move the segment onto the band.

title: Desktop Schedule has no visible or keyboard path to Add shift
what: The band offers only "All locations" and "…", and the "…" menu has no Add shift or Build and publish. The grid's "+ Add" appears only on cell hover and is aria-hidden with tabIndex -1.
why: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard; the main scheduling action is invisible.
fix: Add a white "Add shift" pill in the band (it becomes "Publish N drafts" when drafts exist) and add Add shift and Build and publish to the "…" menu. Keep the hover "+ Add" as a shortcut.

title: Shift requests uses 32px decision buttons on phones and 355px slabs on desktop
what: On phones Decline and Approve are 32px tall with an 8px gap. On desktop the same buttons stretch to 355px each. "Current workflow policy requires manager review." repeats under every row.
why: Fitts's law: the main decisions are the smallest targets, next to each other.
fix: Use the .b-decide pair from inbox-b.tsx:115: 44–48px tall, min-width 96px, right-aligned on desktop. State the policy once under the segment: "Swaps need your approval (Scheduling rules › Trades)".

title: Build and publish hides its week label under the band
what: On phones the "This week · Nov 9 – 15" line is clipped behind the teal band, because the band runs 44px down as if a card came next.
why: Clipped content; DESIGN: "a form's first label or a plain line never lands on teal".
fix: Exclude .c-pub from the 44px band run-on, or move the week into the band as the white sub-line, as Edit shift does.

title: The notification count is drawn five ways, including a red badge
what: Owner and Manager desktop show a red #C8322B numeric badge on the bell; phones show a coral dot; Employee desktop shows a teal count in the sidebar, sometimes as a separate chip under the bell. Employees on tablet see three indicators at once, and the collapsed rail badge covers the Things to do icon.
why: Unread updates are information, not an alarm. One colour, one meaning.
fix: Use a coral dot on the bell and a teal count where a number is shown; remove #C8322B. Anchor counts to the icon's top-right corner, reserve the badge slot so it doesn't pop in, and show one notification entry point per width.

title: On phones the Tab key may never reach page content, and there is no skip link
what: Recorded 390 keyboard walks for all four roles loop tab bar → wordmark → bell → avatar → tab bar without reaching Home content; desktop reaches everything. Phones also hide the skip link.
why: WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.1, if confirmed. The capture may be a harness effect.
fix: Reproduce with a hardware keyboard at 390. If real, make the hidden width variant display:none or inert and keep the visible one out of any inert subtree. Show the skip link on focus at every width.

title: Primary buttons aren't always pills
what: The phone's full-width form primary, the big primary and the payroll ink button are rounded rectangles while desktop and sign-in use pills. Welcome, Find ID and Activate buttons are 12px rectangles, and nine different radii express "pill".
why: DESIGN: primary buttons are teal pills. The most important button changes shape between screens.
fix: border-radius: 999px on .b-btn--full, --big, .b-ink__btn, every chip and every auth button; remove the half-height radii and the desktop override.

title: Desktop sidebar group labels and select placeholders use a decorative grey
what: Sidebar group names are 12px/600 #8C9397 on #FBFCFC (3.03:1); select placeholders and the availability axis labels use the same grey.
why: WCAG 1.4.3: readable text set in a decorative grey.
fix: Point all three at the grey text token #6A7176 (4.85:1 on #FBFCFC).

title: Timecards and Time corrections give recovery steps in audit jargon
what: "Timecards expired. Refresh a current protected snapshot.", "Approve the current source revision before finalizing." and "Retry the same action to reconcile it." Time corrections and exports add "auditable effective adjustment", "canonical time record" and "Historical approval does not release the current assignment".
why: The person can't tell what to press. DESIGN U5: plain language over audit language.
fix: "These timecards are out of date. Refresh to see the latest." / "Approve the latest version of this timecard before finalizing." / "We couldn't confirm that. Try again; it won't be done twice." Apply the same pass to time corrections, attendance review, exports and exchange.

title: Assisted recovery tells employees to open "Reset access", which doesn't exist
what: "Share it privately. They open Reset access, enter the code and choose a new password." No screen has that name.
why: The steps name links that don't exist.
fix: "Share it privately. On the sign-in page they choose Forgot password?, then I have a recovery code, enter it and choose a new password."

title: 44 pages have no page title, so the tab and screen readers say only "NEVORA"
what: My pay, Payroll, Settings sub-pages, Add and Edit shift, Add employee, Updates compose and more fall back to "NEVORA"; with Mobile Access off, every sign-in page reads "NEVORA Workforce".
why: WCAG 2.4.2; tabs and history become indistinguishable.
fix: Give each page its H1 as metadata ("My pay", "Add shift", "Clocker PINs"…) and fall back to AUTH_COPY titles on sign-in pages.

title: Schedule success notes are not announced to screen readers
what: "Shift deleted.", "Shift updated.", "Changes published…" and "Copied 3 shifts…" render through CorpNote, which has no role="status".
why: After a redirect, screen-reader users get no confirmation (WCAG 4.1.3).
fix: Wrap each note in role="status" or give CorpNote an announce prop.

title: Payday countdown and dates disagree because Payroll uses the UTC date
what: One payday (Fri, Nov 20) is 11 days away on Home and My pay but 10 days away on Payroll. It is also styled three ways: amber chip, green chip and grey text. Payroll settings shows a change dated tomorrow.
why: Honest figures (DESIGN "Nothing estimated") and similarity (one fact, three looks).
fix: Derive `today` in the company time zone, as Home does. Format "Change history" in that zone too. Use one payday chip everywhere: amber while timecards wait and green when ready (home-b.tsx:144–146 already has this logic). Reuse it in `payroll-runs.tsx:214` and My pay.

title: At 320, the clamped sub-line hides the schedule-conflict warning that explains "Review"
what: The conflict note (`.b-leave-note`, `inbox-b.tsx:98`) is inside `.b-row__s`. At 359px and below, `src/components/owner-b/owner-b.css:302` clamps `.b-row__s` to two lines. The comment above it says "never cut to '…'", but it does cut.
why: Truncation with no way back (an escalation trigger), and WCAG 1.4.10 reflow at 320.
fix: Render the note as a sibling block of `.b-row__s`, outside the clamped element. Or limit the clamp to the date span: `.b-row__s > :not(.b-leave-note)`.

title: The selected day shows no keyboard focus ring
what: Inside the hero, focus is white (`src/components/owner-b/owner-b.css:29`). The current day tile is white (`owner-b.css:235`), and the ring is inset, so it is white on white. Keyboard users lose their place on the week strip.
why: WCAG 2.4.7 and 1.4.11 (an escalation trigger).
fix: Add `.b-week__d:is([aria-current="date"],[aria-pressed="true"]):focus-visible { outline-color: #0B6E69; outline-offset: -3px; }`, or use offset `+2px` so the white ring sits on the glass.

title: A time-off conflict looks like a normal shift
what: The cell says she is off and also scheduled, with no warning colour. Things to do flags the same shift as "Fill Ana Colon's shift · Needs an Owner".
why: Red = stop and amber = check; state must not rely on reading small grey text; Gestalt figure–ground.
fix: When a cell has leave plus a shift, draw the block with an amber 2px inset ring, an amber `WarningIcon`, and the label "Needs cover". Make it link to the fill flow. Code: `src/components/manager-weekly-roster.tsx:351–352`.

title: The approving state turns the summary into a batch tool the screen doesn't support
what: "0 selected · 3 eligible · 9 excluded · Select up to 100 current timecards below" A "Selected action" select. Disabled "Review selected timecards" and "Retry original attempted action" buttons.
why: Doherty threshold; layout stability; Hick's law; error prevention.
fix: Show batch controls only after the owner chooses "Approve N ready". During a single-card save keep the summary as it was and show progress in the panel button only ("Approving…" with a spinner, in place). Code: `src/components/timecards.tsx:487–518`.

title: Approving a timecard ends on a blank page with no confirmation
what: The summary, table and links disappear, leaving bare canvas. The tabs are dimmed and the panel shows only "Checking period timecards…" in 13px grey. There is no green "Approved" anywhere.
why: Visibility of system status; green = done; Doherty threshold.
fix: Keep the table rendered (stale-while-revalidate). Flip the row's status to a green "Approved" chip immediately, and show a `role="status"` line in the panel: "Elena Ruiz's timecard is approved". Refresh in the background.

title: The Manager loses all navigation in loading, error and offline states
what: While the access check is unavailable, the Manager's tab bar and sidebar collapse to Home only, so a slow network leaves them no way to move. The Owner keeps all five tabs.
why: Navigation must survive a failed read.
fix: Build the Manager's tabs from the last known operational context instead of dropping them when context.operational is unavailable (app-shell.tsx:183–185).

title: Done and older shows its title twice and loses the band header (phone)
what: The phone shows a white header with the dark "NEVORA WORKFORCE" wordmark, the only main-flow page without the teal header. "Done and older" appears white in the band, then again in dark ink straddling the band's bottom edge (contrast 1.1:1 on teal).
why: Figure-ground; consistency with the Direction B hero (DESIGN.MD:1395–1400).
fix: At `src/components/manager-inbox-corp.tsx:258–261`, `moreView` skips `<InboxB>`, so `CorpNav` and `CorpTitle` both render on phones. Render a `BScreen`/`BHero` with back "Things to do" for `moreView`, or give `CorpTitle` the phone-hidden class there.

title: The "Management menu unavailable" card sits above the band, collides with the wordmark, and adds a second refresh button
what: The card renders as the first child of `<main>`, above the hero. It uses the old corp card: 12px radius, 15px title (`src/app/app/corp-shell.css:391–394`). Its "Refresh management access" button competes with "Refresh current view" one card lower. That gives two refresh actions and three explanations of one problem.
why: Figure-ground and overlap; one primary action per view; an error should name one recovery path.
fix: At `src/components/app-shell.tsx:496`, drop the separate section. Let the B route state (`scoped-read-frame.tsx:186–191`) carry one message: "Couldn't check your access." with one action, "Try again", that calls both `operational.retry` and `refreshCurrent`. Show it as a 22px card under the hero, with an amber icon in a tinted circle.

title: The Time off list says "withdraw it", but the request page has no Withdraw
what: The note reads "Open a request to see its details or withdraw it." A waiting request's page ends with "To change this request, contact your manager." and no action.
why: The instruction leads to a dead end; trust.
fix: Either add a red-outline "Withdraw request" with confirmation on waiting requests, or change the note to "Open a request to see its details."

decision.q: Can employees withdraw a waiting time-off request themselves?
options: Yes: add a red-outline "Withdraw request" with a confirm on waiting requests.
No: keep "contact your manager" and remove the promise from the list note.
decision.rec: Allow it for waiting requests. It saves the manager a step and the list already promises it.

title: Requests counts the swap that needs your answer as waiting on others
what: The band shows "Waiting 6 · on your manager or a teammate" and "Needs your answer 1". The six include that same incoming swap, and its row is the only one with no chip.
why: Wrong count; the one item that needs the person gets the least emphasis.
fix: Count Waiting as waiting.length only. Give the incoming swap its own first card with an amber "Needs your answer" chip and the teal Review button.

title: One time-correction flow calls the same thing a fix, correction, proposal and submission
what: Fix my time uses "Fix a missed punch", "Request a correction", "Earlier fix", "Start another proposal" and "Check your original submission" on one screen.
why: The "check earlier submission" recovery depends on knowing which thing to check.
fix: Noun "correction request", verb "Fix a punch": "Your correction requests", "Request another correction", "Checking your request…", "Check your earlier request".

title: "Correction recorded" suggests the change was applied
what: After sending a correction the screen says "Correction recorded", but it was only sent for review.
why: Truthful feedback rule.
fix: "Correction request sent".

title: Employee Home's "See all" opens Notifications, not Things to do
what: "See all" (aria "See all N things to do") under Things to do opens /app/notifications; the Owner's same-named link opens Things to do. Lead Home shows "See all 7" with the same target.
why: Same-named links go to different places.
fix: Make it "See all notifications", or point it at a things-to-do view.

title: Push notifications say "review your pending task" for decided requests
what: Every request decision sends "NEVORA Request Update / Open NEVORA to review your pending task." Other pushes are Title Case ("Your NEVORA Schedule Is Ready", "Coverage Needs Attention").
why: A decided request is not pending, and employees have no "tasks".
fix: "Your request has an update / Open NEVORA to see it."; "Your schedule is ready", "Your schedule changed", "A shift needs cover".

title: Home tells someone who is already clocked in to clock in
what: Time says "Right now · On the clock · Clocked in at 12:02 PM · 9 h 24 min so far". Home's "On shift now" card says "Clock in on the Main Office tablet · Breaks and clock out happen there too". The instruction never changes with the clock state, so Home contradicts Time and can send someone back to the tablet to punch twice.
why: Match between system and the real world; consistency (Jakob's law within the product); honest status.
fix: In `src/components/employee-b/home-b.tsx:122-123`, branch the tinted notice on the punch state. The hero already reads Time's records (`hoursAuthority`), so the state is available. When clocked in: a green dot with "Clocked in at 12:02 PM" and "Breaks and clock out on the Main Office tablet". When the shift has started and there is no punch: an amber "Not clocked in yet" with "Clock in on the Main Office tablet".

title: Fix my time: the first label sits on the teal band and the form isn't one white card
what: "What to fix" (13.5px/600, `#6A7176`) is drawn on the teal band. Its computed contrast is 1.23:1 on `#0B6E69` and 1.16:1 on `#0C726C`. The rest of the form sits loose on the canvas instead of in the lifted white card that DESIGN specifies ("a form's first label or a plain line never lands on teal"; "forms as one white card").
why: WCAG 1.4.3; figure-ground; common region.
fix: Make the card rule match the rendered structure, for example a class set on the form wrapper rather than the `:has` chain. Check in the browser that the white card starts 40px over the hero.

title: On tablets, sign-in titles turn white on the canvas and pages lose their card
what: From 768 to 1023px, "Good evening" and the workspace chip render white on the light canvas (about 1.1:1). Welcome, Access help, Find ID and Activate draw no white card and slide 40px up under the band.
why: Clipped and invisible content at a supported width; WCAG 1.4.3.
fix: Copy the phone rules auth-b.css:196–205 into a (min-width:768px) and (max-width:1023px) block for #mobile-access-page, so the title is ink on the card and the band holds only the top bar and back link.

title: Desktop and tablet back-pages have no language switch or wordmark
what: Forgot password, New password, Activate and Help on desktop and tablet show neither the Español switch nor the wordmark.
why: A Spanish speaker can't switch language mid-flow.
fix: One change in auth-shell.tsx: render the top bar with wordmark and language switch on every auth page.

title: Rail labels never appear on touch, so icon-only navigation can't be learned on a tablet
what: The approved rail relies on "labels as tooltips". `src/components/sidebar-rail-tooltip.tsx:64` returns early when `event.pointerType === "touch"`, and `:84` hides the tip on `pointerdown`. A tablet user therefore never sees a name before committing to a tap. The Employee rail shows FileText (Pay) next to ClipboardText (Requests). Both read as "document".
why: Recognition over recall.
fix: Show the existing tip on touch-and-hold: on `pointerdown` with `pointerType === "touch"`, start the 300ms `RAIL_TIP_DELAY_MS` timer, and cancel it on `pointerup` before the delay. Use the phone tab's icon for the same destination in the rail (`receipt` for Pay at navigation.ts:211). Keep the toggle that opens the full sidebar as the always-available path to labels.

title: At 768 the week grid truncates shift times ("7:3…", "11:…", "11:3…") instead of wrapping
what: The approved rule is "long ones wrap to two lines" (DESIGN.MD:1525; mock frame). At 768, open-shift chips and the today column clip the start time with an ellipsis. There is no way back to the full value without tapping into the shift. The person column stays at 180px, which squeezes day columns to about 64px; the mock assumed 71–81px.
why: Truncated content with no way to reach it (an escalation trigger); closure.
fix: Inside the `@container c-sched (min-width: 560px)` block (owner-b-desktop.css:536), add `.cm-block > span { white-space: normal; overflow: visible; text-overflow: clip }`. Under 820px of container width, take the person column to 148px (avatar plus name on two lines) to return about 32px to the seven day columns.

title: Spanish Clocker shows a wrong generic line for nine server errors
what: Any server error missing from the dictionary falls back to "No pudimos confirmar esta información. Pide ayuda al dueño." Setup-code expiry, "Reconnect this tablet" and seven others have no Spanish entry.
why: Spanish users get a wrong instruction and lose the real next step.
fix: Add the nine Spanish lines, show the English text with lang="en" as the fallback, and add a test that every server error string has a Spanish entry.

title: Spanish Clocker sends employees to the owner instead of their manager
what: "PIN not recognized… Try again or ask your manager" is translated "…pide ayuda al dueño" (the owner).
why: The translation sends the employee to a different person.
fix: "…Inténtalo de nuevo o pide ayuda a tu gerente."

title: Clocker recovery messages use jargon on a shared kiosk
what: "Retry the same action only; it keeps the original request ID", "No action was replayed", "Recovery storage is unavailable" and "photo exception" appear on the kiosk.
why: Kiosk users need one clear step; audit words hide it.
fix: "We haven't confirmed your last punch yet. Tap Retry Same Action; it won't punch twice." / "Nothing was punched again." / "This tablet can't save punches right now. Ask your manager to check the tablet."

title: The live clock is clipped at the band's edge, and AM/PM is lost
what: At 1024 the band is `clamp(320px, 36vw, 480px)` = 368px, which leaves a 296px content box after 36px padding each side. The clock is `clamp(5.5rem, 11.7vw, 8.25rem)` = 120px. "10:43" alone measures about 306px in the shot, and the 30px day period plus the 10px gap add about 55px more.
why: The band's hero figure is the kiosk's primary information (aesthetic-usability.
fix: Size the clock to the band, not the viewport. Add `container-type: inline-size` to `.band` (clocker.module.css:56). Use `.clock { font-size: clamp(4.5rem, 29cqi, 8.25rem); }` (:72). At a 296px content box that is about 86px, so "10:43 p. m." fits. Alternatively, let `.clock` wrap the day period under the digits: `flex-wrap: wrap` on `.clock`, with `.clock > span { flex-basis: 100% }` only when it doesn't fit.

title: The band says "Tablet registered" (green dot) while the card says the tablet is offline, locked or must be reconnected
what: The band's status comes only from the setup check, at `clocker-setup.tsx:80` → `clocker-shell.tsx:30,56`. The PIN gate's failures never reach it, at `clocker-pin-gate.tsx:106–107`. These are a 401 device failure, offline, a 503 and "could not clear verification".
why: One colour, one meaning (green = done or OK) is used against its meaning.
fix: Lift a `tabletHealth` value from `ClockerPinGate` to `ClockerShell`, through a context or an `onStatus` callback. Map 401/device → `attn` "Reconnect needed", offline/503/clear-failed → `attn` "No connection", 429 → `attn` "Paused: too many attempts". `.status[data-tone=attn]` already exists (clocker.module.css:82). Only the text and tone are passed, with no layout change.

title: The empty PIN slots fail non-text contrast, and fail worse in the error state
what: The four slots are the only progress indicator for the PIN. An empty slot ring is `#9AA3A8` on the field's `#F2F5F4`: 2.34:1 (clocker.module.css:221). In the error state it's `#E19A92` on `#FDECEA`: 1.99:1 (:224). At arm's length, under store lighting, the user can't count the digits remaining.
why: WCAG 1.4.11 (meaningful graphics need 3:1). Fitts's and Doherty's laws suffer indirectly: the user re-types because they lost count.
fix: Use `#7A8489` for the empty ring (about 3.6:1 on `#F2F5F4`) at :221. Use `#C2554A` in the error state (about 3.9:1 on `#FDECEA`) at :224. Consider 18px slots with a 2.5px ring.

title: Every blocked PIN state offers the same "Check Connection" button, which doesn't fix three of the four causes
what: `blockedCard` (`clocker-pin-gate.tsx:115–116`) always renders one secondary button, "Check Connection", which calls `reset()`.
why: An error that names no way to recover is an escalation trigger.
fix: `tone === 'device'`: add the instruction line "Ask a manager to set up this tablet again (Settings → Clocker tablets)". Label the button "Check again". `tone === 'wait'`: label the button "Try again", or disable it for 60s. `stop` (offline/clear failed): keep "Check Connection".

title: The PIN lockout covers the whole tablet, but the screen reads as though it's about the next person
what: The attempt budget is per device (`pins.server.ts:62–70`: "Reserve the shared/tablet attempt budget"; scope `DEVICE`). After someone else's wrong PINs, the next employee walks up to "Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes before trying again." The heading is still "Enter your PIN" (`clocker-pin-gate.tsx:125`).
why: Blocks the core task for uninvolved users; mental model (Jakob's law); privacy and fairness on a shared device.
fix: UI only; the server's limits stay as they are. When `tone === 'wait'`, change the heading from "Enter your PIN" to "This tablet is paused". Add a second line: "Too many wrong PINs were entered on this tablet. Wait about five minutes, or ask a manager to record your time."

decision.q: The Clocker PIN lockout is per tablet, so one person's wrong PINs block everyone. Keep that scope?
options: Keep the device-wide lockout (current server rule) and change only the screen: "This tablet is paused" plus "ask a manager to record your time".
Move to a per-person lockout so the next employee can still clock in.
decision.rec: Ship the screen change now; it needs no server work. Then decide on per-person scope with whoever owns PIN security.

title: The privacy pill wraps, overlaps the card and is clipped at phone width
what: `.privacy` is a one-row flex at `width: min(472px, calc(100% - 48px))` (clocker.module.css:247). The button "Continue securely" / "Continue securely" in Spanish ("Continuar de forma segura") takes its full width with `flex: none` (:251). The message is squeezed into the leftover 60–140px.
why: The privacy countdown must be readable in its last seconds. Clipped content is an escalation trigger (better-layout "plan for growth").
fix: Let the pill wrap. Use `flex-wrap: wrap` on `.privacy`, `.privacy p { min-width: 12ch }`, and `.privacy .btn { flex: 1 0 100% }` under `@media (max-width: 599px)`. Use `position: fixed; bottom: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` on phones, so it is always in view. Shorten the line to "Clears in 5 s" (copy owner), or drop the text, since the count ring already carries it, and keep an `.sr` sentence.

title: The photo-path receipt doesn't say what was recorded and looks nothing like the normal receipt
what: After "Photo for Clock Out", the result is a 64px ring with a thin check (not the 96px filled check) and the heading "Time recorded". It doesn't name the action (Clock Out). There is no hero time, no goodbye line and no 8-second bar.
why: Confirmation clarity (the user must see which punch was recorded); a semantic colour used against its meaning (the warning is shown neutral); consistency between states.
fix: Reuse the punch panel's receipt block for `phase === 'complete'`: the `.check`, `.hero`, `.bye`, `.saved` and `.countdown` classes from clocker.module.css. Set the heading from `receipts[state.action]` ("Clock Out Recorded"). Render the photo exception as `.note[data-tone=amber]` with the warning icon. Use the same `clockTime()` format and a `.btn[data-kind=secondary]` "Done".

title: Desktop account activation is hard-coded English inside the Spanish page
what: On a computer, "Account activated", "Invitation verified", "Create password" and "Activate account" stay English while the band, Español toggle and footer are Spanish.
why: A Spanish speaker activating on a computer gets English mid-flow.
fix: Read every string from AUTH_COPY[lang] or MOBILE_ACCESS_COPY[lang], which already have the keys.

title: Spanish sign-in says "el Owner" and "el dueño" on the same screen
what: auth-copy says "con el Owner" and "Pídesela al Owner", while mobile-access, the emails and the Clocker say "el dueño". The login page renders both.
why: An English word inside Spanish copy, inconsistent on one screen.
fix: "el dueño" everywhere (or "la persona dueña del negocio" where gender matters), recorded in the glossary.

title: "Forgot password" opens a page called "Forgot access"
what: The link says "Forgot password?", the page title is "Forgot access" on desktop and "Forgot password." on mobile, and the reset button is "Restablecer" on one and "Cambiar contraseña" on the other.
why: The link and the page it opens should share a name.
fix: Title "Forgot password" / "¿Olvidaste tu contraseña?"; button "Reset password" / "Restablecer contraseña" in both copy sets.

title: The "Contact" heading is clipped behind the band at every width
what: Only the bottom half of "Contact" shows, at y≈205 (1440) and y≈155 (390), sliced by the band's edge and the card that overlaps it. The first group label is unreadable.
why: Content clipped at a supported width (escalation trigger); WCAG 1.4.10.
fix: Drop the "Contact" label, since mock 7 doesn't need it: "Email support" is self-explanatory. Or add `:is(.q-hd) + .q-grp { margin-top: 56px }` in auth-b.css.

title: The legal footer fails contrast on every desktop auth page and every policy page
what: The footer text and its Privacy, Terms and Support links measure 3.16:1 (`#8A8A87` on `#F2F5F4`). Axe reports `color-contrast` (serious) on 4 nodes per page. On policy pages the "· Terms of Use" and "· Support" spans are 3.16:1 too. The links differ from the surrounding text only by a slightly darker grey.
why: WCAG 1.4.3 (body text at 13px needs 4.5:1); WCAG 1.4.1 (links in a line need more than colour).
fix: Use `#6A7176` (4.52:1 on the canvas) for the line and `#3F464B` (8.74:1) for the links, with `text-decoration:underline` on hover and focus. Phones under Mobile Access already pass (`--ma-muted #5F6D68`, mobile-access.css:70), so the tokens can be unified on those.

title: The error state shows "off" copy and puts the error in a teal info note
what: The title is "Setup needs a check" (amber ring). The body is the off text ("Get schedule changes … may ask for notification permission"), because `describe()` has no error branch (`device-settings.tsx:32`).
why: The escalation trigger "semantic colour used against its meaning" (an error in teal = information).
fix: Add an error text in `describe()`: "NEVORA couldn't confirm this phone's alert setup. Check again, or review the app's setup." Render `s.message` inside the card under the text with amber ink for failures (or drop it when it repeats the text). Make "Check again" `kind="teal"` in the error and revoked states.

title: The Owner has no way to reach app alerts inside the app
what: Owner Profile shows Phone, Email, Time zone, Notifications and Privacy. Owner More shows Insights, Updates, My pay, Settings, Help and Sign out. Neither has a row that opens the popover. The account-menu "Device settings" item is hidden on `/app/profile` and is desktop chrome (`src/components/app-shell.tsx:363`).
why: This blocks the task.
fix: Add an "Alerts on this device" row to Owner Profile, shown only under the native user agent, with `popoverTarget="portal-device-settings"`. Focus then returns to that row on Done.

title: Arrow-key selection can leave the visible list
what: The results list scrolls (`portal-gusto.css:392` `overflow-y: auto`; `max-height: min(560px, 100vh − 120px)` at :385). ArrowUp and ArrowDown only change `active` (`command-finder.tsx:157–161`). Nothing scrolls the active option into view.
why: WCAG 2.4.7 (the active row is the keyboard focus here), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured; Doherty (lost orientation).
fix: In `command-finder.tsx`, add `useEffect(() => { document.getElementById(\`command-finder-${current}\`)?.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" }); }, [current])`. Add `overscroll-behavior: contain` to `.command-finder-results` at `portal-gusto.css:392`.

title: The active result is shown only by a 1.15:1 tint
what: `corp-shell.css:695` paints the current option `#E6F1EF` on white, which measures 1.15:1. `:696` then resets the label to ink and weight 400, cancelling the intended teal 600 label at `portal-gusto.css:398`. For a keyboard user this tint is the only position cue.
why: WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (state indicator), 2.4.7 Focus Visible; figure-ground.
fix: At `corp-shell.css:695–696`, keep the fill and add `box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 #0B6E69`. Set the label to `color: #0B6E69; font-weight: 600`. The leading bar alone gives 6.09:1.

title: The phone "Schedule options" sheet renders unstyled
what: Items sit flush at x=0: "This week", "Copy previous week", "Print schedule" and "Settings" touch the screen edge. "Week templates", "Scheduling rules" and "Activity" are indented about 10px. Every trailing chevron wraps onto its own line under the label.
why: Gestalt proximity and continuity (a chevron detached from its label); alignment; aesthetic-usability. This is the main scheduling screen.
fix: In the B phone sheet, style the menu's group labels as the B section label: 13.5px/600 grey, 16px inset, 20px above. Style items as one flex row: 52px, 16px sides, label then value then a trailing 18px bold chevron, with hairlines between rows. Reuse the Location sheet's row rule for the `b-schedule-more-actions` popover.

title: The time-off date field hides what a keyboard user types
what: `PickField` lays a transparent native `<input type="date">` over a fake "Choose date" span (`employee-mobile/timeoff.tsx:24–35`). Keyboard Tab enters the month, day and year segments, but they are invisible. The field still reads "Choose date" while digits are typed, until a full valid date exists.
why: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions; Doherty (no feedback).
fix: When the input has `:focus-visible` (keyboard), show the native control. Add to `requests.css`: `.tof-pick:has(> input:focus-visible) > span { visibility: hidden } .tof-pick:has(> input:focus-visible) > input { opacity: 1; color: #111517 }`. Or replace the overlay with a visible button that calls `showPicker()`, plus a real text field fallback.

title: About 3,900 !important rules and fake-id selectors make every fix risky
what: owner-b-desktop.css is 98.7% !important, and about 1,025 fake-id :not() steps ladder up to 8 ids of specificity to beat earlier rounds.
why: Any polish change must out-escalate the ladder, so a fix on one page breaks another.
fix: Put each era in a cascade layer (@layer base, signature, clean, corp, quiet, b) imported from layout.tsx, then remove !important and fake ids file by file, starting with owner-b-shell.css.

title: A saved dark-theme preference can still turn on dark styles with no way back
what: Direction B is light only, but THEME_SCRIPT still reads localStorage 'nv-theme', so a device that saved dark gets data-theme="dark". Quiet elements then turn near-white on B's white cards, and no theme control remains.
why: Possible invisible text on Settings, Profile and policy pages (not verified in a browser).
fix: Make THEME_SCRIPT always set light and clear nv-theme; delete Quiet's and Signature's dark blocks.

title: Hours, durations and time ranges are written many different ways
what: One week's hours read "436.5 h", "86 h", "87 h", "86 h 51 min" and "20 h 32" depending on the screen. Ranges appear as "7:30–9 PM", "12:00 PM – 8:00 PM", "12–7 AM", "midnight – 7:00 AM" and "11:30a – 7:30p", sometimes on adjacent rows.
why: Similarity and the approved Nov 7 rule: period totals are whole hours ("511 h"), rows are "24 h 06".
fix: Add one shared formatter in the kit with three outputs: totals "437 h", rows "8 h 06", sentences "1 h 30 min". Add one range formatter: full times, a spaced en dash, U+202F before AM/PM, "midnight" or "12 AM" chosen once. Keep the compact form only in the dense grid. Retire hoursText decimals and compactRange.

title: Times and units break mid-value when lines wrap
what: Shift times wrap as "12:00 PM – 11:30 / PM" at 320 and 768, "11:30a – / 7:30p" on the 1280 grid, and inbox titles leave "– 12 AM" alone on a line. "11.5 / h" and "Respond by / Nov 18" also split.
why: The most important figure on Home breaks inside a time. DESIGN's narrow-phone rule: a title's parts wrap whole.
fix: Wrap each <time> and each "N h" in white-space: nowrap (or join with U+00A0) so the only break is at the en dash. Drop the 32px hero time to 26px below 360px and below 820px.

title: The back link and the highlighted tab name different places
what: Clocker recovery says "‹ Settings" while Team is lit. Pick up and swap says "‹ Schedule" while desktop lights Requests. Activity says "‹ Schedule" on a Home URL, and tablets show "‹ More" with no More in the rail.
why: Jakob's law and wayfinding: people lose their place when two cues name two parents.
fix: Derive the back label and the lit tab from one parent map in src/lib/navigation.ts. Map every /app/exchange* route to Schedule on desktop, /app/clocker-recovery to Settings, and on tablet hide "‹ More" or name the lit rail entry.

title: Status colours change from screen to screen
what: An open shift is amber on Home and grey "Not filled" on Schedule. "Published" is green on one screen and grey on Build and publish. Timecard status is a chip on phone and coloured text on desktop, "Working" is grey text on Team and a green dot elsewhere, and finished setup steps are teal.
why: One colour, one meaning: red stops, amber waits or checks, green is done, teal is information.
fix: Add a status-to-tone table in the kit (BChip tone by status key) and route corp and Quiet pills through it. Grey only for neutral facts. Specific swaps: Published green, open shift amber until it ends, done steps green #1D6B45, live state a green dot.

title: Over-target and over-plan hours look normal
what: "56 h of 40 h · 16 h over" uses the same grey line as "On target". Insights draws 86 h worked against 48 h planned as a calm, full teal bar, with "38 h over plan" in small grey text.
why: Overtime risk is the reason these views exist. Amber means check.
fix: Show an amber "16 h over" chip on over-target rows and a grey "8 h under" chip on under-target rows. On Insights, cap the planned part at 100% in teal, draw the excess amber and add an amber "+38 h over plan" chip.

title: The live tiles put an amber dot on "Late 0" and none on open shifts
what: "Late 0" carries an amber status dot while "Open shifts 3", the figure that needs action, has none.
why: Amber draws the eye to a non-problem. Status dots must follow the value.
fix: Set the dot from the value: amber when late > 0, none at 0, and amber on Open shifts when gaps exist.

title: Pages load through an old-style skeleton, then jump
what: While a page loads, phones show the retired white "NEVORA / WORKFORCE" header and a warm Quiet skeleton with no band. Then the 128–308px teal band drops in and everything jumps about 300px. Employee Home shows only "Loading your shift..." and rebuilds its title, eyebrow and cards when data lands.
why: Layout shift and a "two apps" flash on every tab tap (aesthetic-usability, Doherty).
fix: Under [data-nv-b], render the B band at the route's final height plus 22px card skeletons in #ECEEEF from the frame's checking branch. Keep the top bar identical in both states and use "…".

title: Error, empty and loading states come in seven shapes, none with an icon or colour
what: Errors appear as a hero sentence with a grey button, a card with a ghost "Try again", centred text with a grey pill, or a plain note. None has an icon or amber cue, the message often repeats in the band and the card, and Lead loading uses a disabled "Checking…" button as a spinner.
why: Similarity and status colour: an error looks like an empty state. Jakob's law.
fix: Build one BStateCard: a 48px icon circle (grey loading, amber offline or paused, red failed), a 16/22 title, one line, a teal recovery pill, left-aligned. Say the state once, keep the page's own primary action, and use skeleton rows for loading.

title: The in-app 404 on phones is still the old corporate page
what: At 390 the in-app 404 shows a white header, the dark two-line wordmark, a teal numeric bell badge and the title on the canvas, with no band and no tab lit. Desktop already has the band.
why: DESIGN lists the 404 under Direction B (teal band, lifted card).
fix: Render src/app/app/not-found.tsx through BScreen and BHero ("Page not found", back to Home) with the card holding "Go to Home". The public 404 stays as is.

title: The Time off list hides the staffing conflict that Things to do shows
what: On Time off, Maria's and James's waiting requests look like the other five, with no "On the schedule" warning and no Decline or Approve, though approving them leaves a shift uncovered. Approved rows show grey text instead of a green chip.
why: Same item, different information by screen; the risk is hidden where the decision is made.
fix: Reuse the Things to do row: the amber conflict line plus compact Decline and Approve. Show a green "Approved" chip on decided rows.

title: Row buttons in Things to do change weight by position, not meaning
what: The first "Find cover" is solid teal and the next two are pale, though all three are today. Conflicted rows say "Review" and others "Approve", so Decline edges misalign, and Employee Home stacks four equal teal "Review" pills in one card.
why: Similarity and "fill exactly one action per view": identical actions read as different states.
fix: Give every row in a group the same button kind (code uses kind={index === 0 ? "teal" : "ghost"}). Use a fixed min-width of 96–104px so edges line up. On Employee and Lead Home render each to-do as one BRow with a chevron and an amber status chip, and keep one teal button for the most urgent item.

title: Swap and Can't-work rows in Things to do omit the other person and the actions
what: A swap row shows only "Ana Colon · Tue, Nov 17 · 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM" with a chevron. Shift requests shows the same item as "Swap Sat, 12:00 PM with James Ortiz" with Decline and Approve.
why: Consistency across screens; the decision needs the counterpart.
fix: Use the exchange sub-line ("Swap Sat, 12:00 PM with James Ortiz") and the same compact Decline and Approve pair as Time off rows.

title: Time corrections make the reviewer find the change themselves
what: Each request stacks three equal grey boxes, Recorded, Current effective and Proposed, and Recorded and Current are often identical. The actual change (2:06 PM → 2:41 PM, +35 min) gets no emphasis, and four grey helper lines follow.
why: Visual hierarchy: the one fact that matters has the same weight as the rest.
fix: Show two tiles, Recorded and Asked for, with the changed time in bold and a "+35 min" chip. Show Current effective only when it differs. Fold the helper lines into one secondary line and put the reason in a labelled quote.

title: Prepare payroll offers one action four ways and puts the future first
what: "Prepare payroll" appears as a teal text link, a full-width teal button, a text link "Prepare" and "Choose dates" on one page. The future period sits above "2 periods with no payroll", whose alert gets the weaker button, and "Close" is ambiguous.
why: Similarity and Hick's law; the overdue work should lead.
fix: Order overdue periods first. Give the oldest the only filled pill and the rest a quiet "Prepare" pill of the same size. Replace "Close" with a chevron disclosure.

title: Recent payrolls show grey money, bare icons and an unmarked replaced run
what: "Oct 19–25" appears twice (correction and original) with no link between them and no "Replaced" chip. Amounts are grey (4.26:1), and receipt icons are bare glyphs here but tinted circles on Payroll.
why: Money is the key figure; similarity across sibling lists.
fix: Nest the original under its correction as "Replaced by correction". Set amounts in ink 600, right-aligned, tabular. Wrap icons in the 36px tinted circle.

title: Punch photos shows child switches on while the main switch is off
what: "Take punch photos" is off, yet Clock in, Start break, End break and Clock out are bright teal and on, so you can't tell whether photos will be taken.
why: Parent-child state must read at a glance.
fix: When the parent is off, indent the children with aria-disabled and the disabled token pair, or hide them until it is on.

title: Week templates' only action looks disabled
what: "Save this week" is the grey quiet pill, the same family as disabled buttons, and it repeats the heading. "No saved weeks yet" floats as a grey caption on the canvas.
why: One filled action per view; an enabled action must look enabled.
fix: Make it the teal pill "Save template" under a "New template" card title, and move the empty state into a card with a tinted icon and one line of purpose.

title: Locked fields look like empty or editable inputs
what: Edit shift shows Location as a grey field with no lock or reason, and the Clocker key sits in a white bordered input identical to Name. Three read-only treatments are in use.
why: Affordance: a field that looks editable but isn't wastes a tap.
fix: Use the Company profile pattern everywhere: a value row with a 16px bold LockSimple and a one-line reason ("Location is set when the shift is created").

title: The Edit shift title is indented 25px from its own sub-line
what: On desktop and tablet the H1 "Edit shift" starts about 25px right of "Published · Wed, Nov 25" and the content column. Add shift, with no sub-line, aligns correctly.
why: Alignment to shared edges.
fix: Zero the inline offset on .c-shift__titles > .c-shift__title; the order:-1; flex:1 rule at owner-b-desktop.css:196 hits the column wrapper. Or add align-items: flex-start at :488.

title: Schedule grid names wrap while day columns have room
what: The person column is about 180px, so long names wrap and rows balloon, while each day column has 40–60px unused.
why: Layout balance; row height should follow content.
fix: Give the name column minmax(200px, 1.4fr) and days minmax(0, 1fr). Clamp names to two lines with the full name in title and the accessible name.

title: The schedule grid card wastes its first row on a grey "Published"
what: The first 52px of the grid card holds only a grey "Published" at the far right, and "Covered this week" sits 350px from its tiles.
why: Published is the done state (green), and the header is prime space.
fix: Put a green "Published" chip in the band beside the week stepper, delete the empty row, and stack the "Covered this week" label above its tiles.

title: Every day in the phone week strip has the same amber dot and no legend
what: An amber dot under every day marks open shifts, but with all seven marked and no legend it carries no information; the meaning is only in the aria-label.
why: Signal-to-noise; a mark on everything marks nothing.
fix: Show the open count as a small amber number under the date, or a dot only when the day is under target, and add a one-line legend "• Open shifts".

title: /schedule/coverage lands on the grid with an unrelated error inside the band
what: The coverage route redirects to /app/schedule?error=INVALID_SHIFT and shows "Couldn't open that shift", though no shift was picked. The pink banner sits inside the teal band and pushes the stepper down 64px.
why: A broken route plus an error that names the wrong cause.
fix: Route coverage to the open-shifts view. Show route errors under the band as a white note with a red icon in a tinted circle and a dismiss control.

title: Desktop Team loses the phone's filters and status chips
what: Phones filter "All 12 · Working 4 · Late 0 · Off today 4" with status chips. Desktop has neither: "Working" is grey text, rows have no chevrons and "See all" has no count.
why: Parity: the Manager's quickest attendance check exists only on the phone.
fix: Add the filter tabs to the desktop band, render status as a green chip with the live dot, add trailing chevrons, and say "See all 12".

title: A person's page shows an internal ID and offers little else
what: The meta line shows "ID QA-SCAN-A" in the most-read spot, Call and Message are 40px rounded squares, positions wrap over three lines, and rows carry no preview of shifts or hours.
why: Hierarchy: show what a manager needs, hide internals.
fix: Move the ID into Access and sign-in. Use 44px tinted circles in 48px targets. Show positions as chips and add Today and This week values to rows.

title: The request detail is split into four cards and loses its status colour
what: One time-off decision spreads over four cards, with Decline and Approve floating on the canvas and a centred note. On the Employee side the list's amber "Waiting" chip becomes plain ink on the detail, and the header leads with "Sent Mon, Nov 9".
why: Common region and status colour; the date requested should lead.
fix: Use one request card (dates as the title, reason, also-off) and one conflict card whose footer holds the actions. Lead the status with the amber Waiting chip.

title: The desktop live-figure strip stops short of the card grid
what: At 1440 the glass strip ends at x 1215 while the cards and the band's white action end at 1376, because .b-live is capped at 920px.
why: Alignment to shared edges.
fix: Use max-width: none so the strip spans the grid, or size it to the grid's own width token.

title: Desktop Home leaves a large empty block under the main card
what: "Needs you 16" shows 3 rows and ends at y≈562 while the right column runs to y≈997, leaving about 700×350px of empty canvas. The Lead grid leaves a 130px hole under Today's team.
why: Balance and use of space; the primary card is the shortest.
fix: Show up to 6 rows at ≥1024px (rows.slice(0, 3) at home-b.tsx:128) and say "See all 16". Let the Lead's right column flow on its own.

title: Some pages put their title on the canvas under an empty band
what: Update detail and Profile shrink the band to a back bar and set the title in ink on the canvas at 24–26px, so the title jumps place and size between pages. Titles now sit in three places.
why: Continuity between sibling pages.
fix: Use one BHero rule for all phone secondary pages: title in the band, with date or meta as the band sub-line.

title: "Needs reply · 1" is not marked on any update
what: The Updates segment promises one update needing a reply, but all rows look the same.
why: A filter count with no matching cue.
fix: Add an amber "Needs reply" chip to that row and use the shared count style ("Needs reply 1").

title: Sign out is red
what: The account menu and More pages show "Sign out" in red #B42318 for Owner, Manager, Employee and Lead.
why: Red means stop or destructive; Sign out competes with Delete account.
fix: Use ink or teal text for Sign out and keep red for Delete and Turn off.

title: More and Settings rows drop the tinted icons other lists use
what: More, Settings and Help rows are plain text, while Team and Timecards rows lead with a 36px tinted icon. On phones, Insights, Updates, My pay, Settings and Help live only behind the avatar.
why: Similarity: DESIGN rows carry "face or 36px tinted icon".
fix: Give each navigation row its Phosphor bold icon in a tinted circle and end every tappable row with a chevron. Add a small "More" cue beside the header avatar.

title: Profile deep links all land on the bare Profile
what: /app/profile/privacy, /terms, /calendar and /passkeys open the plain Profile with nothing expanded, and the "Security" section holds only Delete my account.
why: Deep links from Help and notifications should land on the thing named.
fix: Open the matching section on load, and rename "Security" to "Account" while it holds only deletion.

title: Disclosure rows use a pale right chevron that means "go to a page"
what: Help, Profile, Who's working and the policy pages expand in place behind a right chevron, which elsewhere means navigation. The caret is #B5BBBF or #B8B8B5 (1.9–2.0:1), though it is the only open/closed cue.
why: WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast; DESIGN round 4: "Help, Calendar and Privacy open with the same grey down caret".
fix: Use CaretDown bold 16px #6A7176 for every disclosure, rotating up when open. Keep CaretRight only for rows that navigate.

title: Save sits in a different place on every form
what: Settings forms put Save on the band, in a card footer, or floating on the canvas below the card. On tablets full-width bars stretch to 726px, and Availability always shows a disabled full-width Save.
why: Jakob's law: people look for Save in one place.
fix: Long settings pages: Save on the band. Single-card tools: right-aligned 48px pills in the card footer. Nothing floats on the canvas. Show Availability's Save only when something changed.

title: Segmented controls come in three styles
what: Page filters appear as glass on the band (Things to do, Timecards), grey on the canvas (Notifications, Availability) or as underline tabs, with three corner and thumb geometries. On desktop the thumb renders squashed.
why: One component, one look.
fix: One segmented control: track 14, thumb 10, padding 4, 36px thumb with a 44px hit. Every page-level filter sits on the band on glass; keep underline tabs for in-card sub-filters.

title: Rows signal "opens" and "expands" inconsistently
what: Timecard rows with hours have no chevron while "No time yet" rows do, yet both open the sheet. Team, Approved requests and Availability rows open with no chevron, and timecard status is plain coloured text.
why: Affordance and similarity; the rows worth opening look static.
fix: Trailing CaretRight for navigation, CaretDown for disclosure, no chevron where the action is a button. Render status with the chip component. Fix chevron={!hours} at timecards.tsx:571.

title: A person's face tint changes between screens
what: Requests, Shift requests and Availability draw every face teal, Things to do gives James Ortiz purple, and the same person is teal on Profile and peach on More.
why: DESIGN Nov 7: "a person keeps one face tint on every screen".
fix: Replace .q-av initials with BAvatar (faceTint(name)), or apply faceTint inline on .q-av. Keep the header treatment for "me".

title: Grey secondary text sits just under AA on tinted fills and Quiet rows
what: Secondary lines measure 4.26–4.41:1 on grey fills and tinted notes, and Quiet and corp row meta reads 4.30:1 on Requests, Shift requests, Profile, Settings and Payroll history. The public legal line is 3.16:1.
why: WCAG 1.4.3.
fix: Add --b-grey-on-fill #5E666B for grey text on tints (already used in clocker.module.css:179). Point .q-rt i, .q-rv, .c-row__value--soft and .c-row__detail at #6A7176 under [data-nv-b], after confirming the rendered pair in a browser.

title: The Home week chart has no values, scale or caption
what: Seven bars sit under single letters (two Ts, two Ss) with no values or axis, and only today's bar is dark, so it reads as the only one that counts.
why: A chart nobody can read adds no information.
fix: Use three-letter days, print each day's hours above its bar in tabular figures, add a caption ("Scheduled hours by day") and an aria-label listing the values. Or drop the chart.

title: "Covered this week" fills two of three tiles with "—"
what: Positions and Lead tiles show a big ink dash with "No positions required" and "No lead required", placeholder content in prime space.
why: Show what is configured.
fix: When a requirement isn't configured, collapse the tile into one grey line under Staffing ("Positions and leads aren't required · Set up").

title: Activity lists tomorrow above today and fills up with to-dos
what: "Tue, Nov 10" coverage gaps sit above "Today · Mon, Nov 9". Ten of twelve rows are coverage gaps (a to-do list) in grey, though they are amber in Things to do.
why: Order and meaning: a history should show what happened.
fix: Show events that happened, Today first. Put any gaps in a "Coming up" group with amber icons and link once to Things to do.

title: The workplace name is cut off in the account menu and sidebar
what: The 240px account menu and the sidebar workspace tile both ellipsize the workplace name with no tooltip or second line.
why: People need to confirm which workplace they're in.
fix: Let the menu header wrap to two lines and widen it to 280px; give the sidebar chip a title and a second line "Owner · 2 locations".

title: ARIA names sit on generic elements and inbox forms become duplicate landmarks
what: aria-label is set on a plain div in Updates compose and on chip spans in b-kit, which screen readers ignore (axe serious). Each time-off row's <form aria-label> adds a form landmark, seven per list.
why: WCAG 4.1.2; landmark navigation clutter.
fix: Add role="group" to the feedback div or use a labelled section; move chip meaning into .b-sr text; remove the row forms' aria-label.

title: Forms flag only some empty fields, in three voices
what: Fix my time marks only Location and disables Send; New location flags Short name but not Name; Request time off squeezes "Choose a valid start date." into a 157px column and leaves "To" unmarked. Messages come from three systems, and none has an error icon.
why: Error prevention and recovery: people fix one field, retry, and find the next.
fix: One pattern in form-validation.tsx: mark every invalid field with aria-invalid and an inline message with a warning icon, focus the first, keep Send enabled. Split combined errors by cause and place them beside the field.

title: Content and the band's main pill end at different right edges
what: On desktop, cards, the live strip and the band's white action end at three different x positions, and the 812px reading column sits under a band whose action is pinned to the 1080px edge. The band action also moves between pages.
why: Alignment to shared edges; the main action should not jump.
fix: Pin the band action to the content column's right edge on every page width.

title: Fields and selects are drawn many ways, with edges almost invisible
what: Field edges are #D5DADC at 1.41:1 on white, drawn three ways. Selects come in heights 32–52px, radii 8–14px, text 14–17px and four carets in two weights, and date inputs miss the 14px corner rule. On iPad, 14px select text may trigger zoom.
why: WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast; the same "choose one" control looks different on every form.
fix: One field token at 3:1 (#8C9397) drawn as border: 1px solid. One select spec: 48px, radius 14, 16px text, one bold 16px caret via mask-image in currentColor, teal 2px focus edge. Apply by element in the shared layer, and keep 16px text under pointer: coarse.

title: The teal band is painted with seven recipes and varies in height and lift
what: Seven teal and three ink band gradients exist, though DESIGN names one (#0C726C to #08504C), so the band's hue shifts between pages and sign-in. On phone forms the band is 92–112px tall and cards lift 28px on some pages and start 16–32px below on others.
why: Continuity; the lighter #0E7A74 start also pushes band text under AA.
fix: Define --b-band and --b-band-ink once and reuse them in every layer. Use one sheet-band height (92px) and one lift (band runs 44px under, card overlaps 28px) for every page whose first child is a card.

title: Tabular figures space out hyphens on desktop and tablet
what: Desktop and tablet inherit tabular-nums for the whole page, so "clock‑out", "sign‑in", "555‑0100" and "back‑office" render with spaced hyphens. The phone opts in only for numbers, and its tab-badge selector never matches.
why: Counts and times change width between phone and desktop; text looks broken.
fix: One rule in the shared kit at every width: normal on the page root and tabular-nums only on number classes (.c-num, .b-live__v, td, time, counts and badges). Delete the scoped copies.

title: The hero date looks like a button but does nothing
what: The date on Home's hero is a span styled as a glass button, and it gets the press scale.
why: A dead button on the main screen.
fix: Give it a non-button glass text style, or make it the date picker it suggests.

title: Navigation, menus and the desktop bell use regular-weight icons beside bold content
what: Phosphor is the only icon set, but the tab bar, sidebar, rail, desktop bell, menus and the password eye use regular weight beside bold page icons. Chevrons come in five sizes and the sidebar icon size depends on role.
why: The shell looks thinner than the content; DESIGN standard is Phosphor bold.
fix: Default NavIcon to bold with fill when active, use bold BellIcon on desktop, pass weight="bold" in action-menu and auth controls, and use three sizes: 16, 18 and 20.

title: The same place or thing has two to five names
what: Things to do is also "To do" and "Needs you"; Team is also "Employees"; Timecards is also "Time"; Can't work appears in five forms; withdrawing is "Cancel request", "Withdraw" or "Cancel report"; "On the clock", "Working", "On shift now" and "Clocked in" mean one state.
why: One word per concept; the nav comment promises "each label is the page's own title".
fix: Adopt the glossary below: Things to do (tab To do), Team, Time off and time-off request, Can't work, Withdraw request, Clocked in, Pay statement, Shift lead, workplace. Update voice.md and the QA scripts that press these labels in the same change.

title: One failure has four headings, and some error titles name pages that don't exist
what: A failed page says "This page could not be loaded", "We couldn't open this page", "Couldn't load this page" or "This page couldn't load." Insights errors say "Reports unavailable" and Time exports "Payroll exports unavailable"; the 404 has three headings.
why: One message, one next step.
fix: "This page didn't load" / "Nothing was changed. Check your connection, then try again." with "Try again" and "Go to Home". "Page not found" for every 404. Error titles use the page's own name.

title: Confirmations promise delivery or don't say what happened
what: "Time off approved. The employee will be told." and "Each person with a change has been notified." promise pushes that may be off. "Action recorded" and "The request was reviewed." don't say what happened.
why: Truthful feedback rule; say what changed.
fix: "Time off approved. {Name} will see it in Requests." / "Changes published. Each person with a change can see it in their schedule." / "Payroll approved", "Time off declined".

title: Owner settings use audit words: revision, retained, scope, operational, receipt transport
what: Company policies say "Retained request saved as revision 4. Current selected revision 5."; manager access says "Receipt transport unavailable" and "Revoke this Manager's operational access?"; invitations say "Revoke invitation".
why: Plain language; confirmations should name the person and the consequence.
fix: "Your earlier save went through as version 4. You're now viewing version 5." / "Remove {Name}'s manager access? They keep their employee account." / "Cancel invitation: the link in their email stops working."

title: Owner Home and lists show unclear counts and dead-end empty lines
what: The stat says "Late" while the row says "3 missed clock-ins"; the filter shows "All 0" when the total is unknown; "Things to do isn't available right now." and "No one right now." give no next step or subject.
why: Unknown must not read as zero; empty states say what is empty.
fix: One name for the stat and row ("Missed clock-ins"); "All" with no number when unknown; "Things to do didn't load. Try again." with a button; filter-aware empty lines ("No one is late.").

title: Payroll settings copy is audit language, and it is locked
what: "Native statements publish automatically after generation and verification", "neutral payroll import", "Neutral instructions · compatibility unverified" and "owner-authorized provisional policy… does not establish statutory compliance" appear in main text.
why: Plain language; DESIGN.MD:1320 marks payroll copy as locked.
fix: With Jose's sign-off: "Pay statements are published to employees after you approve payroll." / "Payment file format" / "Not yet tested with your bank" / "Bank and file type", then a full payroll copy pass.

decision.q: Payroll copy is locked (DESIGN.MD:1320). Can it be rewritten in plain language?
options: Unlock it for a supervised plain-language pass, with Jose approving each line.
Keep it locked as-is until a legal or accounting review.
decision.rec: Unlock it for a supervised pass. Start with the four labels above, which change no legal meaning.

title: Decline sends immediately, 8px from Approve, with no undo
what: Each pair is two 50%-wide pills 8px apart. Decline submits the form at once (`inbox-b.tsx:116–121`). A mis-tap declines a person's time off with nothing to recover it on this screen.
why: Fitts's law (adjacent opposite actions), and the escalation rule for consequential actions.
fix: After Decline, show a 6-second "Time off declined · Undo" notice (`role="status"`, held while focused) before the request is committed, or open a one-line confirm sheet. Approve can stay one-tap.

title: The hero pushes today's shifts below the fold
what: The location chip, week strip and the three "Covered this week" glass tiles fill about 80% of the first screen. The tiles repeat Home's "This week" card.
why: Fitts and Doherty (the main task is a scroll away), and redundancy.
fix: On phones, collapse "Covered this week" to one glass line ("Staffing 57% · 192 h of 336 h"), with Positions and Lead only when required. Or move the tiles under the day's list.

title: Filter chips are small, and the last one is cut off with no fade
what: The chips are 32px tall. At 390, "Off today 4" touches the card's right edge with no end padding. At 320 it is cut to "Off to", with no fade to show the row scrolls.
why: Fitts's law, and the "hint at hidden content" rule.
fix: Give `.b-filters button` (`owner-b.css:173`/`:278`) a `::after { inset: -6px 0 }` hit extension. Add 18px end padding. Add a 24px right `mask-image` fade when the row overflows.

title: Unknown values render as a 2.29:1 dash
what: "Late clock-ins —" and "Cover filled —" are the values in their tiles, at 2.29:1.
why: WCAG 1.4.3.
fix: Colour `.c-stat__value--none` in `#6A7176` (4.96:1 on white), and keep `aria-label="Not available"`.

title: Help's expanded answer is larger than its question
what: The question "I can't sign in" is 15.5px; the answer below it is 17px with a 17px underlined link. The header row also gets a grey fill.
why: Visual hierarchy (the answer outranks its question).
fix: Set answers at 15px/22px `#3F464B` in the row's text column, and keep the header row white with a down caret.

title: Clocker PINs has an unsorted list and a non-standard search position
what: The 12 people are listed in no visible order (Ana, Daniel, Valeria, Sofía, Jose, James, …), while Team sorts alphabetically. The search field and the No PIN/PIN set segment sit on the canvas. On Team, search sits on glass in the hero.
why: Miller's law (scanning an unsorted list), and consistency.
fix: Sort by name, and move search and segment into the hero as on Team.

title: Shift blocks carry no state or position
what: Every assigned block is the same grey pill with a time. Draft and published can't be told apart, and the position is missing. The mock has a legend (Published teal, Draft grey, Open amber) and a position line ("Cashier").
why: Gestalt similarity; recognition over recall.
fix: Use teal-50 with teal text for published, grey for draft and an amber dashed outline for open, plus a 12px position line. Add the three-chip legend to the card header where "Published" sits alone today.

title: The person column leaves 600px between name and hours
what: At 1440 the name ends at x≈450 and Recorded starts at x≈1050, so the eye loses its row.
why: Gestalt proximity; line length.
fix: Add the mock's columns (position under the name, an Attention column), or cap the table at 860px like reading pages. Add row hover `#F7F9F9` (under `@media (hover:hover)`) so the row stays traceable.

title: The issue panel is a dead end
what: The amber "Needs attention · Correction awaiting review" note says to resolve corrections, the Approve button is disabled, and there is no link to the correction.
why: Error recovery; Fitts.
fix: Add a teal pill "Review correction", linking to `/app/timecards/corrections#<id>`, inside the amber note. Keep Approve disabled under it.

title: Settings hub cards touch the band edge
what: The cards start at y=150 and the band ends at y=154, a 4px overlap. That is neither the 24px gap of secondary pages nor the 52px lift of main screens, so the edges look misregistered. The two columns end at x=1352, a third right edge (see OD-076).
why: Gestalt figure–ground; the approved spacing rule (DESIGN Nov 6: "content 24px under the band").
fix: Give the band 28px more bottom padding (lift 52px), or start the grid 24px below it. Set the grid max-width so it ends at 1376 like Home.

title: Phone and desktop show different content for the same page
what: Desktop hides Attention 4, Team filters and Add shift; Time puts the live state second on desktop and shows "Your corrections" only on desktop; Insights Export is desktop-only.
why: Consistency across devices: the same person switches between them.
fix: For each B screen, list the phone hero figures and actions and make sure desktop renders each. On Time, make Right now first and add Your corrections to the phone page.

title: Role-gated pages either explain or silently redirect to Home
what: Payroll and Settings show a notice card to Managers, while Clocker PIN, the requests hub, My time and Profile sub-routes silently redirect to Home or Profile.
why: Predictability; silent redirects look like broken links.
fix: Route every gated page through OwnerOnlyNotice with a lock icon in a tinted circle and one way back.

title: The Owner-only notice is a bare text card with no one to ask
what: The title is body-size (15px bold) with no icon in a tinted circle. DESIGN uses that pattern for every row and state. "Ask an Owner" doesn't name the Owner (Jose Natal is in the Team list) and offers no way to contact them. The only button is "Back to Home", which duplicates the band's back link.
why: An error or denied state should name a way forward; Hick's law (two identical exits); consistency.
fix: Add a `LockSimple` bold icon in a grey-tinted circle and a 17px title ("Payroll is for Owners"). Use the body "Jose Natal can give you payroll access." (pass owner names from the layout). Make the action a teal pill "Message Jose" (Updates compose or a `tel:` link), and remove "Back to Home".

title: The Manager reviews their own and the Owner's time with no "You" or "Owner" marker
what: Elena's own row looks identical to her reports' rows. The copy audit (M-section) notes that another manager must approve her timecard, but nothing on the row says so. The Owner appears first on Hours this week, out of alphabetical order.
why: Scoped data must read as scoped; Gestalt similarity misleads.
fix: Add a grey "You" chip on the current user's row and replace its action with "Another manager approves yours". Tag the Owner row "Owner" and sort alphabetically (`manager-dashboard.tsx` hours list), or exclude Owners from Manager hour targets.

title: "Request not available" names a way back but gives no button
what: The card says "Return to Time off to review your requests" as plain text with no button, while the back circle says "Requests" and opens the hub.
why: An error with no way forward.
fix: Add a quiet pill "Back to Time off" (/app/requests) and the shared state icon.

title: Request lists are not in date order
what: Waiting time off lists Nov 26, then Nov 30 – Dec 2, then Nov 10, so the soonest request is last. The hub, Time off and My requests all show this.
why: Predictable order; the nearest date needs action first.
fix: Sort waiting requests by start date ascending and decided ones by decision date descending before rendering.

title: The Updates search starts 20px inside the band's text edge
what: On desktop and tablet the search field starts at x 316 while the title and back link start at 296; the phone margin survives.
why: Alignment to shared edges.
fix: Add margin-inline: 0 to .eb-tools from 768px (employee-b-desktop.css:243).

title: "Action needed" is amber on one notification and grey on the rest
what: Only the first Team update gets an amber icon circle; the "Schedule update · Action needed" rows stay grey. Five rows say "Schedule update" and never name the subject.
why: One colour, one meaning; rows can't be told apart.
fix: Set tone = required ? 'amber' : 'grey' for every kind (messages-b.tsx:110) and show the subject in the title ("Schedule for Nov 16 – 22 changed").

title: Delete account differs by role and nests a card inside a card
what: The Owner's consent is a toggle and the Employee's a checkbox; the "access ends" icon is teal for one and red for the other. On desktop "Confirm it's you" is a white card inside a white card, and the main action floats outside the card.
why: Consistency; a switch implies an instant setting, not an acknowledgement.
fix: One flow: checkbox consent in a 44px label row, a red-tinted "access ends" icon, a red pill for the enabled destructive action, fields inside a single card.

title: Policy pages run about 105 characters per line and hide their action
