what: Desktop policy paragraphs span about 740px at 15px. The only action, "Review deletion request", is a grey slab on a grey canvas (about 1.0:1), and the contents list doesn't look clickable.
why: Readable measure (45–75 characters); the action must be visible.
fix: Set max-width: 68ch on policy paragraphs and list items. Put the action in the reading card's footer as a white pill, and style the contents entries as teal links or drop them.

title: Focus rings are clipped on live tiles and card corners
what: On desktop live tiles only the leading edge of the focus ring shows, because .b-live clips its children and the ring is inset. Rings on a card's first and last rows are cut by its corners.
why: WCAG 2.4.7 (one edge remains, so Medium).
fix: Use an inset box-shadow ring with position: relative and z-index: 1 on .b-live__a, and border-radius: inherit on first and last row rings.

title: Week-card chips vanish on their block and make block heights ragged
what: "Tomorrow" is a teal-50 chip on a teal-50 block, so the pill disappears. Blocks with two chips stack them on two lines and grow about 30px taller than the rest.
why: Figure-ground and alignment.
fix: Give chips inside .eb-wsh a white fill, and put status and lead chips in one flex-wrap row with a 4px gap so every block keeps one height.

title: Desktop card headers and bodies use different insets
what: Desktop cards put the header at 22px and the body at 18px, and padded text blocks sit 4px inside the row text edge.
why: One text edge per card.
fix: Use one 22px inner inset for header, rows and text blocks on desktop.

title: Employee screens use internal words: planning, eligibility, source, recorded
what: "Checking your current planning…", "Eligibility unavailable", "Your current access or this source changed" and "Submission recorded" appear on employee screens.
why: DESIGN U5: plain language.
fix: "Loading your time off…", "We couldn't check these shifts", "This update changed. Refresh to see the latest.", "Sent. Refresh to see its status."

title: The in-app Español option and the onboarding guide suggest Spanish that isn't there
what: Profile's language row offers English and Español "For the sign-in pages", but every signed-in screen stays English. The onboarding guide renders in Spanish inside the English Home.
why: Mixed languages on one screen; a setting that seems to do nothing.
fix: Say "Sign-in pages only. The rest of NEVORA is in English for now." and render the guide in English until B5 ships.

title: Desktop Schedule shows the same week twice
what: "Your week" lists all seven shifts, and "Coming up" lists the same seven again as rows. "7 shifts · 59.5 h" appears in the band sub and again in the week card's footer. The right column is empty below y=700.
why: Redundancy hurts scanning (Miller's law); desktop use of wide space.
fix: On desktop, drop Coming up, or limit it to today and the next shift. The week card already holds the rest. Move "Confirm this week" and "Open shifts" to the top of the right column. Keep only the publication sentence in the week card's footer.

title: Desktop demotes the one required action
what: Confirming is the only thing the manager asked for, and on desktop it appears after both the week card and the row list starts.
why: Order by importance; phone and desktop parity; Fitts's law (distance from the band where the eye lands).
fix: Put the Confirm card at the top of the right column, level with the week card. Put "Confirm week" as the band's white pill (the band is empty at the right apart from Availability).

title: Confirming gives almost no feedback and the layout jumps twice
what: While pending: the button moves under the text, becomes a pale "Confirming…" pill and adds "Checking the current schedule confirmation…". The card grows from 83 to 153 CSS px. The card and the "What changed in your schedule" card both disappear, and everything below shifts up.
why: Visibility of system status; continuity; feedback must leave a static cue in place.
fix: Keep the button in place with its width while it spins. On success, morph the card into a green state: check in a tinted circle, "Week confirmed", "Mon, Nov 9 · 9:41 PM". Keep it for the session. Keep the "What changed" disclosure.

title: The phone shift sheet's actions don't use the Direction B icon treatment
what: "Swap with someone", "Offer for cover" and "I can't work this shift" are regular-weight Phosphor glyphs with no circle on phones. The desktop panel draws them in tinted circles, red for "I can't work".
why: Similarity; the DESIGN rule "Phosphor bold icons in 36px tinted circles"; phone and desktop parity.
fix: Move the circle rule out of the desktop layer into `employee-b/schedule.css`, and add `weight="bold"` to the three icons.

title: Two competing titles, and phone and desktop pick different ones
what: On the phone, the 30px H1 "Pay" is followed by a 34px "Fri, Nov 20", so the date outranks the page title. On desktop the H1 is visually hidden and the date is the band's title. The audit finds `h1 "Pay"` with no visible counterpart.
why: Visual hierarchy; heading level matches size; consistency.
fix: Title "Pay", with the date as a figure (28/34) under "Next payday · in 11 days"; or. Drop the visible "Pay" on the phone as desktop does.

title: "Correction" and "Replaced" statements look identical
what: Two rows read "Fri, Nov 6 · For work Oct 26 – Nov 1" with grey chips of equal weight. Nothing shows which statement is current.
why: Visual hierarchy; figure-ground.
fix: Show the correction as the normal row with chip "Corrected". Show the replaced one muted: grey text, chip "Replaced", sub "Replaced by the Nov 6 correction". Alternatively, nest it under the correction.

title: The hub and Time off disagree on what is waiting
what: The two screens list different waiting time-off requests from the same run. Status: Not verified. It may be a fixture added between captures (the scan-leave-maria request is Nov 10). Worth checking the hub read's limit and filter.
why: Consistency of counts.
fix: Confirm that the hub's waiting read returns every waiting time-off request, or say "Showing 2 of 3".

title: Dotted lines start or end with "·", which breaks the Nov 7 rule
what: DESIGN round 4 says a dotted line "never starts or ends a line with a ·".
why: Typography: wrap at segment boundaries.
fix: Render both through `Dotted`. For the shift line, put the date as the title and "7:00 AM – 3:00 PM · Main Office" as the sub.

title: The empty-state link says "phone" on desktop and leads to a dead end
what: On desktop the Requests empty state links "Get alerts on this phone", and it leads to "Your workplace hasn't turned on device alerts".
why: Information scent; no dead-end calls to action.
fix: Say "Get alerts on this device". Hide the link when the workplace has alerts off; the alerts page already knows this state.

title: Delete account is a form but keeps the tab bar and header icons, and disables its button until valid
what: DESIGN: "forms … hide the bell and avatar; forms also hide the tab bar". Here both remain, and the tab bar lights Home. "Delete my account" is a pale pink disabled pill (2.37:1) until the password and checkbox are filled. The checkbox is 24×24 (audit).
why: Consistency with the form pattern; validate on submit; Fitts's law.
fix: Hide the tab bar and header actions on `/app/account/delete`. Keep the destructive button enabled, and show errors on submit. Make the whole checkbox label row the 48px target.

title: "Message today's team" has up to three entry points on Lead Home
what: Desktop Lead Home offers the same message action in the band, in Today's team and in a row; phones show two adjacent ones.
why: Hick's law; one action, one place.
fix: Keep one entry point in the Today's team card ("Write") and drop the duplicates.

title: The "On shift now" content is shown twice and takes the whole first screen
what: The hero's first glass figure reads "On shift now / 12–11:30 PM / Shift lead · Customer Support". Directly under it, the first card has the same title, "On shift now", and the same range in a different format: "12:00 PM – 11:30 PM".
why: Redundant information.
fix: Keep the approved hero figure. In the card, when `now && lead`, keep only the chip and drop the sentence, by gating `eb-leadline`'s text on `!now` (`src/components/employee-b/home-b.tsx:121`). Retitle the card "Your shift" so it doesn't echo the figure (`home-b.tsx:116`).

decision.q: Lead Home repeats "On shift now" three ways. The extra sentence is in the Nov 8 Lead spec. Trim it?
options: Drop the sentence when the hero already shows the shift, retitle the card "Your shift".
Keep the Nov 8 spec as written.
decision.rec: Trim it. Things to do moves back onto the first phone screen.

title: Today's team (a Lead extra) sits above Things to do on phones
what: The phone order is shift card, publication note, Today's team, Things to do (7, with deadlines), Coming up. A self-started, optional action (messaging the team) outranks items that carry "Respond by" deadlines. On desktop the team card is in the right column, so it doesn't compete there.
why: Order by importance.
fix: Render `TeamCard` after Things to do on phones (`home-b.tsx:197`). Desktop keeps it in grid column 2 through `employee-b-desktop.css:406`, which is unaffected because grid placement is explicit.

title: Coming up drops "Shift lead" on today's and tomorrow's shifts
what: Mon 9 (which Home calls "You're the shift lead today") shows only "Now". Tue 10 shows only "Tomorrow". Wed–Sun show "Shift lead". Home's Coming up shows "Shift lead" on Tue 10, so the same shift is marked on Home and unmarked on Schedule.
why: Consistency.
fix: Move "Shift lead" into the sub-line ("Shift lead · Customer Support · Main Office") so it never competes with the time chip, or allow a second chip at ≥390px (`employee-schedule-corp.tsx:134`, `home-b.tsx:153`).

title: "Request time off" changes place, and disappears in the loading, error and offline states
what: On the phone Time off page, the action is a teal text row at the foot of the list card. On the Requests hub (phone) and on desktop, it is the band's white pill. In the three state captures the row is gone, so a Lead can't start a request while the list fails, even though the form doesn't depend on the list.
why: Consistency of the primary action's position.
fix: Render the white band pill on the phone Time off page as well, outside the list read (`timeoff-b.tsx`; the state card at `:114`).

title: The tab that needs an answer has no badge on phones
what: Desktop tabs read "Open shifts · 2 / For you · 1". Phone tabs read "Open shifts / For you / My requests" with no count, so the swap waiting on the Lead is invisible from the default tab. On desktop, Open shifts loses its "· 2" once another tab is selected.
why: Visibility of system status, consistency across widths, and Fitts's law (34px targets against a 48px+ target).
fix: Show the count on phones, at least an amber dot on "For you" when it holds a needs-answer item, and keep the counts on every tab. The tabs are 36px in the kit (`owner-b-pages.css:56,90`; segment geometry is S5 in the design-system audit). Give the phone segments a 44px hit area.

title: The compose action differs in icon and place between Home and Updates
what: Updates draws compose with a pencil (band button and phone row, `src/components/employee-b/messages-b.tsx:134,155`). Home draws it with a megaphone (`home-b.tsx:101,190`). On the phone Updates page, "Write an update" is the last row of the "Earlier" card, below the read items, while on desktop it is the band's primary.
why: Gestalt similarity across screens, and a primary action buried at the end of a list (serial position).
fix: Use the pencil everywhere for compose and keep the megaphone for updates. On phone, put "Write an update" in the band as a glass pill (the same slot as Schedule's "Availability"), not at the list foot.

title: Hover tints stick after a tap and sometimes match the canvas
what: 20 hover rules sit outside @media (hover: hover), so on iPad and phones rows and arrows stay tinted after a tap. Row hover uses five tints, one equal to the canvas, so a single-row card loses its edge.
why: A latched hover looks like a selection.
fix: Wrap hover rules in @media (hover: hover) and use one --b-hover #F7F9F9 inside white cards.

title: At 768, This week wraps and leaves a dead area under Payday
what: "192 h of / 336 h" "No / positions / required" (three lines) "No lead / required"
why: Gestalt common region and closure (the row reads unfinished); aesthetic-usability.
fix: Under 900px, put the three Covered-this-week tiles in a one-line compact form (value plus a one-word label, e.g. "57% staffing", with "No positions required" moved to its tooltip or a footnote), or stack them two plus one. Give the row `align-items: stretch`, and pin Payday's button to the card foot so the two cards end together.

title: The week card truncates every role and location, then repeats the full text below
what: "Customer S…" and "Main Office…" at 900 become "Custom…" and "Main Of…" at 768. The audit's `clipped` list confirms ellipsis on 4 frames. The Coming up list right below shows the same seven shifts in full. The card's 14 truncated lines add noise without information.
why: Miller's law; aesthetic-usability; similarity.
fix: From 768 to 1023, show only time plus a status chip in the week blocks and drop the role and location lines (Coming up carries them). Use one time format for the card and the list.

title: Focus styles vary between fields, links and forms
what: Fields use an outline, an inset shadow or a border change; phone sign-in uses blue and teal rings on one form; the Clocker's text-link ring is square and touches the button above; the rail badge covers the ring.
why: One focus language.
fix: outline: 2px solid #0B6E69; outline-offset: 2px on every field. Confirm teal for sign-in with Jose and set --ma-focus. Give .link border-radius: 999px and more top margin; raise the focused rail link's z-index.

title: Clocker icons mean two things: one coffee cup, one hourglass
what: Start Break and End Break use the same coffee cup, and one hourglass means both "locked out" and "in progress".
why: Each headline glyph should mean one thing.
fix: Use a coffee cup for Start Break and an arrow-back or play glyph for End Break; keep the hourglass for progress and a lock or pause glyph for lockout.

title: Buttons press with three scales and four speeds, and disabled ones still shrink
what: Press feedback is 0.96, 0.97 or 0.98 at 120–160ms with three easings, so the same teal pill presses differently on Things to do and a request page. Some disabled controls still scale on press.
why: A disabled control that moves suggests it worked.
fix: One guarded rule: :is(.b-btn, .c-btn, .q-btn, .wc-btn):not(:disabled, [aria-disabled=true]):active { scale: .96 } at 150ms ease-out; remove the corp and Quiet transforms under [data-nv-b].

title: Clocker wording: literal Spanish, Title Case drift and joined fragments
what: Spanish uses "acción de tiempo" for a punch and masculine-only "¿Listo para tu foto?". Buttons beyond the six approved Title Case words are Title Case; "Reference: 30 min" reads as an ID; "Saved at" + time + ". This screen clears…" is joined from fragments; "Connect tablet" and "Tablet registered" use two verbs.
why: Natural Puerto Rico Spanish and one voice on a shared kiosk.
fix: "marcación" ("Verifica tu marcación"), "¿Todo listo para la foto?", sentence case outside the exempt words, "Suggested: 30 min", one placeholder string "Saved {time}. This screen clears in 8 seconds.", and "Register tablet". Update QA scripts that press these labels.

title: A kiosk with a broken link gets one action, "Go to sign in"
what: The amber hint ("Is this a time clock tablet?") is the right message. The only button, though, invites whoever is standing at the shared tablet to sign in to NEVORA. An employee arriving to clock in will tap the one teal pill, which leads nowhere useful and puts a personal sign-in on a shared device.
why: Jakob's law (a kiosk error page should not route to an account flow). One primary action per view should be the right one.
fix: When the hint shows (`src/app/not-found-hint.tsx:9`), demote "Go to sign in" to a text link. Make the hint the card's lead, with "Ask a manager to set up this tablet again" as the instruction. Fix the script-tag warning, so the dev overlay isn't mistaken for a product badge in QA shots.

title: In a bright store the keypad grid nearly disappears
what: Key fill `#F0F2F3` on the white card is 1.12:1 (`--ck-key`, :19, :231). The Clear and delete keys have only a 1.5px `#E1E5E6` line, at 1.27:1 (:233). The PIN field's fill `#F2F5F4` on white is 1.10:1 (:216).
why: Fitts's law (a target you can't see is effectively smaller); Gestalt figure-ground; aesthetic-usability.
fix: Darken `--ck-key` to `#E6EAEB` (1.22:1), or add `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #D3D9DB` to `.key`. Raise the tool-key line to `--ck-field` `#D3D9DB` at 2px (:233). The teal pressed tint (`#CFE7E3` with a 2px ring, :234) already reads well.

title: The PIN field looks the same focused and unfocused
what: At rest the field already has a 2px teal inset ring (:216). Focus only thickens it to 3px (:219), and `.pin input:focus-visible { outline: none }` (:218).
why: WCAG 2.4.7 in practice (a 1px change is not a perceivable indicator); better-accessibility "visible focus rings".
fix: Give the resting field a neutral ring, `inset 0 0 0 2px var(--ck-field)` at :216. Keep teal for `:focus-within` and add an outer ring: `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--ck-focus), 0 0 0 4px rgb(11 110 105 / .18)` at :219.

title: A wrong PIN moves the keypad under the finger
what: The error paragraph is inserted between the field and the keypad (`clocker-pin-gate.tsx:135`). That pushes the whole keypad down 27–31px and re-centres the card vertically. The user's next tap, already in flight, lands one row off.
why: Fitts's law; Doherty's law (stable layout during feedback); the "high-frequency interactions get no animation or shift" rule.
fix:
Reserve the message line permanently: render the `

` always, with `min-height: 2.8em` (two lines at .9375rem/1.4), and empty its text when there's no error. Keep `role="alert"` on a stable container, so screen readers still announce it. Alternatively, place the message above the field, under the heading, where no target sits.

title: The red error state stays on while the next PIN is typed
what: `key()` updates the digit count but never clears `error`. `shown = error && !blocked` (:112) keeps the field red, with "PIN not recognized…", while the user enters a new PIN. The newly filled dots render teal on a red wash. The mock describes the red as the response to one submit, not a mode.
why: Status colour semantics (red = stop on an input that is now valid); the field's state doesn't match reality.
fix: In `key()` (:83) and the input's `onChange` (:132), call `setError(null)` on the first keystroke after an error. The message can fade out under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.

title: "Checking…" appears at the very bottom of the card, far from where the user is looking
what: After Continue, the keypad dims to .45 and the only status line is placed below the language toggle (`clocker-pin-gate.tsx:145`, `.busy` :193). It sits about 500px from the field the user was watching. The card also grows 17px and shifts up. The Continue button stays grey with no busy state, so the eye gets no feedback at the point of action.
why: Doherty's law (feedback must sit where attention is); Gestalt proximity.
fix: Put the busy state in the Continue button itself: label "Checking…" plus the 16px spinner. Keep the `role="status"` line, but render it as an `.sr` element so it doesn't change the layout. Optionally show a spinner in the field in place of the dots.

title: In portrait, the wrong-PIN card runs off the bottom of a 768×1024 tablet
what: Key height `clamp(72px, calc((100dvh - 690px) / 4), 96px)` (clocker.module.css:95) is sized for the resting card. The 27px error line (CK-009) then pushes the card past the viewport, and a kiosk without visible scroll hides the language switch and the card's foot.
why: Better-layout ("never park a control where content growth clips it").
fix: Reserving the error line (CK-009) fixes this too. Otherwise subtract it from the clamp: `calc((100dvh - 730px) / 4)`.

title: Two privacy timers disagree, and two private screens show none
what: The static line (`clocker-punch-panel.tsx:219`, `clocker-pin-gate.tsx:123`) keeps saying 30 seconds while the pill counts down. Choose a Break and Clock Out? still belong to the 30s private window. They can be wiped without any reminder until the last 10s.
why: Consistency between states; visible system status.
fix: Hide the static `.clears` line while the pill shows: `.content:has(> .privacy) .clears { visibility: hidden }`. Render the same `.clears` line on `select-break` and `confirm-out` (`clocker-punch-panel.tsx:222–236`).

title: The privacy countdown is announced every second
what:
The `

` text changes on each 250ms tick that crosses a second, so screen readers queue 10 announcements. It is also mounted already containing its text at the 10s mark, which some readers skip.
why: Better-accessibility "announce dynamic content" (stable region, no chatter).
fix: Keep the visible count `aria-hidden`. Render an always-present empty `.sr` status region. Write to it once at 10s ("This screen clears in 10 seconds") and once at 3s.

title: The Spanish receipt puts the date in English order and lowercase
what: `clockTime()` assembles `${month} ${day}` by hand (`clocker-punch-panel.tsx:26–30`). The es-PR locale gets month-before-day and a lowercase "nov". "a las" also precedes a date. The copy audit covers the fragment join; the ordering bug is in code.
why: Better-typography "language and bidi behaviour" (never reorder by hand); the Spanish layout.
fix: Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {month:'short', day:'numeric'}).format()` for the date part, which gives "9 nov". Join it with the time using " · ". In Spanish the result reads "9 nov · 10:47 p. m.". English is unchanged.

title: On Retry, the punch and the exit are identical grey pills with uneven spacing
what: "Retry Same Action" sends a time punch. "Return to PIN" abandons the screen. Both are `.btn[data-kind=secondary]` grey pills of the same size. The gap between them is 22px, versus 12px between Check Action Status and Retry. That's because `leave` renders in its own `.stack` with `margin-top: 22px` (`clocker-punch-panel.tsx:250–255`, css :187).
why: Gestalt similarity and proximity; Hick's law (three pills plus a link in an error state).
fix: Render `leave` inside the same `.stack` as the state's actions, so all gaps are 12px. Style "Return to PIN" as a `.link` (text), as "Cancel & return" already is in the photo flow. The two pills then mean "act" and the link means "leave".

title: Opening "Help with a saved action" stretches the page past the viewport and moves the band clock
what: The panel (`clocker-recovery.tsx:20`) lists every saved reference on the tablet. Each one is a 36-character monospace UUID with its own full-width "Copy reference" pill. On a locked kiosk there is no app to paste into, so the copy action is dead weight.
why: Doherty's law and layout stability; Hick's law; privacy minimisation.
fix: Give the panel `max-height: 40dvh; overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain` (`.handoffPanel`, :321). Show the current person's reference first and collapse the others behind "+2 more". Drop "Copy reference" when `navigator.clipboard` is unavailable, or always on the kiosk, and keep "Ask Owner to review".

title: Sign-in headings end in periods, and the Spanish slogan is a different line
what: "Set up your account.", "Sign in.", "Forgot password." end in periods, against voice.md. English says "Brighter work ahead." while Spanish says "Tu día empieza aquí.", though DESIGN requires the exact slogan from brand.ts.
why: The file is marked "frozen v1" and the slogan is a brand decision.
fix: With approval, drop the heading periods (metadata already strips them) and put one approved Spanish slogan in src/lib/brand.ts.

decision.q: The mobile sign-in copy is frozen v1. May we drop the heading periods, and what is the Spanish slogan?
options: Unfreeze for these two changes: no periods on headings, and a single approved Spanish slogan in brand.ts.
Keep v1 as-is, and record "Tu día empieza aquí." as the approved Spanish slogan.
decision.rec: Drop the periods (matches voice.md and the page titles) and approve one Spanish slogan; a translation of "Brighter work ahead." keeps the brand line identical.

title: Spanish sign-in translations change meaning or gender
what: "Set up your account." becomes "Activar cuenta."; "Soy un empleado nuevo" and "Soy el único dueño" assume gender; "Trabajo no disponible" reads as "no work available". Policy links in Spanish open English-only pages without warning.
why: Translations must match meaning; mixed languages need a warning.
fix: "Configura tu cuenta", "Crea tu contraseña", "Soy nuevo en el trabajo", "No hay otro dueño", "No pudimos cargar tu lugar de trabajo", and add "(en inglés)" to policy links.

title: Account recovery copy uses "channel", "authority" and "portal sessions", and one email names the wrong helper
what: "If… its registered recovery channel is available, recovery instructions will be sent" and "Authority must be verified before any account change" are passive jargon. The recovery email tells Manager and Owner accounts to ask a manager, who can't recover them.
why: Plain language; the email sends people to the wrong person.
fix: "If the details match an active account, we'll email recovery steps. Can't use that email? Ask your manager or Owner for help." Email: "Manager and Owner accounts need another Owner." Subject: "Reset your NEVORA password".

title: The wrong-password error doesn't mark the fields, has no icon, and differs between phone and desktop
what: Neither field gets a red edge. The mock draws both fields red and an icon in the note ("both fields get a red edge"). On phones the note is inset 20px on each side, so it's narrower than the fields: at 390 the note spans x 56–334 while the fields span 36–354. At 320 ES it wraps to three lines in a 208px box.
why: Gestalt similarity: the same message looks different.
fix: Render `aria-invalid="true"` on both inputs when `params.error` is set. That also lights the existing label rule at mobile-access.css:157. Set the alert's margin to 0 inside `.ma-card`. Add a Phosphor `WarningCircle` (bold, 20px) at the start of the note.

title: Empty submit shows the browser's own bubble, in English on the Spanish page
what: The native "Please fill out this field." tooltip appears with an orange "!". On the ES desktop page it is in English. It covers the "Contraseña" label. It isn't Direction B styling, and it bypasses the inline validation the portal uses (DESIGN.MD:86, `form-validation.tsx`).
why: Jakob's law and consistency: the rest of NEVORA validates inline.
fix: Add `noValidate` to the sign-in, recovery and reset forms (login/page.tsx:41, recovery-views.tsx `<form className="q-auth__form">`). Then reuse `form-validation.tsx` so "Enter your Employee ID" / "Escribe tu ID de empleado" shows under the field, in red with the red edge from PB-002, and focus moves to the first empty field.

title: Spanish desktop: the two links under Sign in break into ragged two-line pairs
what: Inside the 336px card column, the links break as "¿Olvidaste tu / contraseña?" and "Activar / cuenta". The first starts at the field edge and the second floats near the centre. They look like two orphaned blocks, not a link pair. In EN they fit on one centred line (public-login-1440.jpg).
why: Gestalt continuity and proximity; translation growth (better-layout, "plan for growth").
fix: Put `white-space:nowrap` on `.q-auth__links a` and `flex-wrap:wrap; row-gap:8px` on `.q-auth__links`. Each link then stays whole, and the pair stacks centred when it doesn't fit.

title: Phone sign-in drops the greeting and leaves the band empty
what: The teal band is a 120px strip holding only the wordmark and Español. The card's title reads "Sign in." with no greeting, and the workspace is a grey chip inside the card.
why: Aesthetic-usability (the arrival moment is flat); conformance to the approved direction.
fix: This needs Jose's call; mock 7 open question 2 is still unanswered. The likely answer is the mock: put the greeting and the glass workspace chip on the band, and leave the card with no title or a quiet "Sign in" label. If "Sign in." stays, record that DESIGN.MD:1537 is superseded for Mobile Access.

title: The password eye is off-system and announces its state twice
what: The eye is Phosphor regular at 22px in `#6B6B6B`, the Quiet grey (audit: `button.q-in__eye` colour rgb(107,107,107)). Direction B uses Phosphor bold and grey `#6A7176`. The label swaps between "Show password" and "Hide password", and `aria-pressed` toggles too. A screen reader announces "Hide password, toggle button, pressed", which is a double negative.
why: Similarity: the icon family and weight differ from the rest of the app.
fix: Use `weight="bold"`, size 20, colour `#6A7176`. Keep a constant `aria-label="Show password"` with `aria-pressed`, or keep the swapping label and drop `aria-pressed`. One mechanism, not both.

title: Desktop's secondary actions don't match the phone, and the disclosure has no cue
what: Desktop shows "I have a code" and "Can't use your email?" as plain teal text at weight 400. The second is a `<details>` summary with no chevron, so nothing says it opens in place. The phone shows "I have a recovery code" as an outlined pill and "Can't use your email?" with a chevron.
why: Similarity: the same action looks different by width.
fix: Add a `CaretDown` (bold, 16px) to the summary and rotate it when open. Include `.q-btn--quiet` in auth-b.css:80 (weight 600). Render "I have a recovery code" as the outlined pill on desktop too.

title: Desktop hides the password rules in a placeholder
what: The phone shows the subtitle "Use the recovery code you received.", the hint "Paste the complete code…" and a live two-rule checklist. Desktop has none of these. The rule exists only as the placeholder "At least 8 characters", which disappears on the first keystroke.
why: Miller's law: don't make people remember the rule while typing.
fix: Render the phone's `AccessPasswordPair` rules (password-pair.tsx:20) and the code hint on desktop too. Label the eye "Show passwords" when it controls two fields.

title: The "no invitation" state is two different screens
what: The card has a back link "‹ Sign in" and also a grey `#F0F2F3` rectangular "Back to sign in" button (12px radius, not a pill). Both go to the same place. A 13px grey footnote reads "No invitation? Ask your Owner." A teal "Get invitation help" button (12px radius) and an "Already activated? Sign in" link.
why: Hick's law: two controls with one outcome.
fix: Use one content model at every width: title, line, the teal pill "Get invitation help" (it moves the task forward) and the link "Already activated? Sign in". Drop the duplicate grey button. Raise the note to 15px `#6A7176`.

title: The illustration sits in the card, and desktop shows two slogans
what: Mock 7 puts the illustration in the teal hero on phones ("its dark edges are transparent, so it melts into the teal") and in the brand panel on desktop. The card is meant to hold only the slogan and the two ways in. The build puts it inside the card, which makes the card 684px tall at 1440. The two buttons are pushed below 580px.
why: Figure-ground (two focal points); Hick's law; conformance to mock 7.
fix: Desktop: move `.ma-welcome-art` into `.q-auth__brand` on `/welcome` and hide the panel line there. Phone: render the art in the band above the card.

title: The topic list doesn't use Direction B icons or containers
what: The icons are Phosphor regular at 20px, bare: black on desktop, teal on phones. Direction B uses bold icons in tinted circles. On desktop the list is a 1px-bordered box inside the white card (card in card). The row descriptions are 13px on desktop but 15px on phones.
why: Similarity with the in-app row pattern; common region (one container is enough).
fix: Use `weight="bold"` in a 36px `#E8F3F1` circle with a teal glyph, as on in-app rows. Remove the `.ma-choices` border inside the card at 1024px and up. Use 14–15px descriptions at every width.

title: "Find your Employee ID": the link sticks out past the text edge, and Sign in appears twice
what: "Activate account" / "Activar cuenta" starts at x 832 while the title, copy and button start at 852. It's 20px outdented. "‹ Sign in" (back) and the teal "Sign in" button both go to `/login`. The button has a 12px radius, not a pill (see PB-035).
why: Align to shared edges; Hick's law.
fix: Add `.ma-text` to the list at mobile-access.css:126, or remove every 20px inset and let the card's 32px padding set one edge. Keep one "Sign in": the button.

title: Policy pages carry no NEVORA brand at all
what: The band holds only "‹ Sign in", the title and the date. There's no wordmark at any width. Mock 7 shows the wordmark on the policy band, and the 404 has it. A legal page reached from an app store or an email shows no product identity.
why: Aesthetic-usability and trust; Jakob's law (legal pages carry the brand).
fix: Render the white `BrandWordmark` (112px, as in not-found.css:48) above the back link, linking to `/login`.

title: On desktop the contents list repeats the accordion line for line
what: "In this policy" lists the same 12 headings that the card beside it lists, with every section closed. The reader scans 24 labels to find one. On Account deletion it's 5 and 5. The contents links jump to `#…-text` inside closed `<details>` and rely on the browser opening them (legal-document.tsx:85).
why: Hick's law; Miller's law; redundancy without information gain.
fix: From 1024px, render the sections open (`<details open>`) as one continuous reading card and keep the contents list as navigation. Collapsed accordions stay on phones and tablets. Alternatively drop the contents list where there are 6 or fewer sections (Account deletion). This changes an approved Nov 8 small round, so it's Jose's call.

title: Phone rows are inset twice and wrap needlessly
what: Row text starts 56px from the screen edge: 16px gutter, 20px list, 20px row. The chevron sits about 37px from the right edge. At 320 the text column is about 190px wide.
why: Align to shared edges, with one spacing step per nesting level.
fix: Inside `.q-doc__list` set the row padding to `0 18px` and remove the extra list inset. That aligns the text with the band title (36px at 390), as on in-app cards.

title: The response promise and the safety line are small, wide and unemphasised
what: "We aim to respond…" runs about 120 characters per line at 13px grey across 740px on desktop. The safety line "Never email passwords, codes, bank details or pay documents." looks like boilerplate. The Mail address below is 17px, the largest text in the body, so the hierarchy is inverted.
why: Typography (measure and size floor); visual hierarchy.
fix: `max-width:68ch` and 14–15px `#6A7176` for `.q-help`. Make the safety line a teal information note (`#E8F3F1` wash, `Info` bold icon). Teal is information, not a warning. Set the address to 15px.

title: "Start deletion request" straddles the band edge and is off the title's edge
what: The white pill sits across the band's lower edge, a tangent: pill y 198–241 against the band end at 238 (1440), and 184–228 against 224 (390). Its left edge is at 192 (1440) and 16 (390), while the title starts at 212 and 36. It's 20px outdented. Mock 7 puts it "at the right of the title, as on every Direction B desktop page".
why: Tangency; align to shared edges.
fix: Desktop: place the pill inside the band, right-aligned on the title row (flex row with `justify-content:space-between`). Phone: put it inside the band below the subtitle, with `margin-left:20px` to match the title edge and its bottom at least 16px above the band end.

title: The how-to section starts closed
what: "In the app or on the web" holds the actual steps, but it's collapsed like the rest. Mock 7: "The first section is open because it is the how-to."
why: Progressive disclosure for the task path.
fix: Add `open={doc.slug === "account-deletion" && index === 0}`.

title: The footer is the legacy lockup, with text under 12px and a second wordmark
what: Under the card the 404 repeats the wordmark. This one is grey, with a coloured "Λ" (the old lockup). It has a "Workforce" module line at 11px and two legal lines at 10px (audit `textUnder12px`). It uses warm Signature grey `#6F6C66`.
why: Similarity and consistency.
fix: Replace the footer with `<QuietLegal lang=…/>` at 13px `#6A7176`, and drop `AuthBrand`, since the band already carries the white wordmark.

title: Desktop auth pages and every policy page don't render Inter
what: On a Mac or iPhone, desktop sign-in and the policy pages render SF Pro, and the app after sign-in renders Inter. The screenshots were taken on Linux, so they show a fallback and hide the difference.
why: Direction B ("Inter throughout"); aesthetic-usability; similarity across the sign-in to app boundary.
fix: In auth-b.css:12–14 add `font-family: Inter, "Inter Fallback", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif !important;` to `main.q-page.q-auth.q-auth` at every width. Check that `.q-auth__line`'s −0.035em tracking still suits Inter.

title: "Checking" uses the "on" colour
what: While checking, the 64px ring is teal (`#E8F3F1`, `#0B6E69`), identical to "Alerts are on". DESIGN (Nov 9) and the component's own comment say grey for "off or checking". The code is `ring()`: `if (busy) return <Ring tone="teal">` (`src/components/native-shell/device-settings.tsx:70`).
why: One colour, one meaning. At a glance a user reads "on" before the check finishes.
fix: `tone="grey"` for busy.

title: "Paused" tells you to return to NEVORA while you are in it, twice
what: The card says "Device settings paused / Return to NEVORA to check this account and device." with no action. A teal note under it repeats "Return to NEVORA to check this device."
why: Redundancy, a self-referential instruction, and a dead-end state with no control.
fix: Body: "Checking will continue when you come back to this screen." Add a "Check now" teal pill. Drop the duplicate `s.message` for the paused state. Pause on `visibilitychange` and `pagehide` only, not `blur`, or ignore `blur` while an enable request is in flight (`actionPending.current`).

title: Confirmation cards have no heading, and the use-for-account confirm sits beside a live "Turn off alerts"
what: Both confirmations are cards with only body text (the name is `aria-label` on a `div role=group`) (`device-settings.tsx:99-106`).
why: WCAG 1.3.1 and 2.4.6 (a heading for the decision), Hick's law (conflicting choices), and change blindness.
fix: `off = !!s.generation && !review && !p.recover`. Give each confirm an `h2` ("Turn off alerts here?" / "Use alerts for this account?") and point `aria-labelledby` at it. Call `scrollIntoView({block:'center'})` when focusing the confirm (`:154-155`).

title: A left-aligned card title over centred content
what: "This device" is left at the card's text edge. The ring, title, text and pills are centred (`.nd-state { align-items:center; text-align:center }`, `device-settings.css:15`). At 1440 the 440px pill stack floats centred in an 812px card under a left-aligned header.
why: Alignment to shared edges and Gestalt continuity.
fix: Drop the "This device" header in the B view (the state title carries the card), or move "This device" into the centred stack as a small grey eyebrow above the ring (`device-settings.tsx:85`).

title: Denied offers no route to the phone's settings
what: "Permission is blocked / Allow NEVORA notifications in your phone settings, then check again." The only action is "Check again". The user has to leave the app and find the setting alone.
why: Jakob's law. Native apps offer "Open Settings" (iOS `UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`, Android app-notification settings).
fix: Add a teal "Open phone settings" pill above Check again, if the bridge can expose it. This needs a native bridge capability, so it is not verifiable here.

title: On phone the popover slices a row and uses a different status visual
what: At 390 the sheet's top edge cuts through the "Notifications · On ›" row (the row's top half shows above it). There is no scrim on phones, so figure and ground blur and the cut row still looks tappable.
why: Figure-ground and consistency.
fix: Add the light scrim on phones too, or anchor the sheet so its top edge falls between cards (`src/components/portal-device-setup.css:5`). Reuse the `Ring` and `nd-state` block in `NativeDeviceSettingsView`.

title: The only action is Sign out, and the copy confuses Leads
what: The page's filled teal primary is "Sign out". There is no "Open in browser" or "Copy link", so the user's actual next step (continue in a browser) has no control. The text says the app "supports Employee and Owner accounts". A Lead, who uses the Employee screens on the web, reasonably thinks "I am an employee" and won't understand the block.
why: A dead end (Hick's and Fitts's laws: the one big button doesn't serve the goal).
fix: Primary teal pill "Open NEVORA in your browser", which opens the web origin externally through the bridge. "Sign out" becomes a quiet pill under it. Line 1: "This version of the NEVORA app is for employees and owners. Shift leads and managers use NEVORA in a web browser."

decision.q: The phone app blocks Leads and Managers with a Sign out page. Should Leads be allowed in the app?
options: Allow Leads, who use the Employee screens on the web, into the app.
Keep the block, but add "Open NEVORA in your browser" as the primary action and explain that shift leads use the browser.
decision.rec: Allow Leads, since their screens are the Employee screens. Until then, ship the browser button and clearer copy.

title: Counts and some labels are under 12px
what: Six declarations sit under 12px: tab labels 10.5px, tab badges 11px, sidebar counts 11 and 11.5px, chips 11–11.5px, and the grid's .c-ampm suffix at 10.4px.
why: Legibility at small sizes; two count sizes between roles.
fix: Counts 12px/700 everywhere; .c-ampm at 0.85em; tab labels stay 10.5px with the C3 colour fix.

title: Results are silently capped at 6 per group
what: `rankFinder(..., perGroup = 6)` (`lib/finder.ts:114,120`) trims every group. Employees and Leads have 12 pages (`finder.ts:51–63`), so the empty finder shows Home through Requests. Time off, Pick up and swap, Availability, Notifications, Profile and Help never appear without typing.
why: Hick's law is served by grouping, not by hiding; visibility of system status; better-layout "hint at hidden content" (trigger).
fix: Show every own page in the Employee and Lead empty state (12 rows fit). For typed results, add a non-option status line: "6 of 11 people · keep typing". Or add a "Show all people" option that raises `perGroup` for that group.

title: Group names are hidden from assistive technology
what: Group headings are `<li role="presentation" aria-hidden="true">` (`command-finder.tsx:189`). A screen reader hears "Schedule" twice, once for the "Publish the schedule" action and once for the page, with no way to tell an action from a page.
why: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; Gestalt common region is visual only.
fix:
Render each group as `
    • …options…
    • `, with the visible heading as the label. Or add `aria-describedby` on each option pointing at its group heading.

title: Result rows don't use the Direction B row anatomy, and some matches are unexplained
what: Rows are text-only 40px lines. Actions, pages, people and places differ only by a 13px grey header. Direction B rows lead with a Phosphor bold icon in a tinted circle. A keyword-only hit ("Activity" via the `schedule` keyword) shows no match emphasis, so it reads as a wrong result.
why: Similarity and recognition over recall; aesthetic-usability.
fix: Lightning bold for Actions;. File bold for Pages;. Initials (BAvatar tint) for People;.

title: Three menu looks, and the selected-check position flips
what: Account, Location and Schedule options: one white surface, about 12px radius, hairline dividers, 15px/400 ink.
why: Similarity; Jakob's law (one menu idiom); common region.
fix: Add `:not(.cm-insights__menu *)` to the selector at `owner-b-desktop.css:424`. White, 16px radius, `--b-elev-2`, 6px padding;. 44px items, 15px/400 ink, 8px item radius, hover `#F7F9F9`;.

title: ActionMenu "sheet" claims to be modal but isn't
what: With `sheet`, the popover gets `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` (`action-menu.tsx:158–160`) but stays `popover="auto"`. The page behind is not inert, so Tab walks out of the sheet into content hidden under it and the scrim. `aria-modal` tells a screen reader the rest is unavailable when it isn't.
why: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 4.1.2.
fix: For `sheet`, render a `<dialog>` and call `showModal()`, as QuietSheet does. Or set `inert` on `.page-frame` and `.mobile-nav` while it is open and remove it on toggle.

title: One panel, three header and close patterns
what: The same right-hand panel has three title sizes and positions and two close treatments. The phone sheet also drops the "Change this shift" heading and the tinted icon circles that desktop shows.
why: Jakob's law and similarity (a close control should look the same everywhere).
fix: Adopt one B panel header: title 20/26 700 left (T2's sheet-title size). Done is a teal 600 text button with a 44px hit area, top-right, in every role and width. Use tinted-circle icons in the action rows at all widths.

title: The employee modal panel's scrim leaves the top bar looking live
what: The dialog is opened with `showModal()`, so everything else is inert. The backdrop starts at y=64 (`employee-b-desktop.css:146` `::backdrop { inset: 64px 0 0 0 }`). Search, the bell, the account menu and the white sidebar-logo block stay fully bright but ignore clicks.
why: Figure-ground (the dimmed area should be exactly what's unavailable); affordance.
fix: Use a full-viewport backdrop (`inset: 0`), keeping the panel at `top: 64px`. Or make it a non-modal inspector like the Owner timecard panel.

title: The phone shift sheet stops mid-screen when the page is scrolled
what: With the page scrolled to reach a row, the sheet settles with its bottom edge at about 533 of 844px. Schedule rows and the tab bar are visible and dimmed below it, and the sheet's flat bottom edge is exposed. In the reduced-motion runs, with the page at scroll 0, it anchors to the bottom as designed.
why: Figure-ground and continuity (a bottom sheet belongs to the bottom edge).
fix: Reproduce on a device after scrolling the Schedule list. If confirmed, check the scroll lock (`html[data-q-sheet]{overflow:hidden}`, quiet.css:669) against the dialog's containing block, and pin with `bottom: 0; top: auto` under `[data-nv-b]`.

title: There's no keyboard path into the Owner timecard inspector
what: The panel is a non-modal `<dialog>.show()` that deliberately leaves focus on the row (`quiet/quiet-sheet.tsx:47–51`). Its controls (Clock-ins and fixes, Approve timecard, Done) come after the whole table in DOM order. A keyboard user tabs through every remaining row, the "people with no time" row and Time exports to reach Approve. Escape closes it (good).
why: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order; Fitts's law for keyboards (distance in Tab stops).
fix: On a keyboard open (Enter on the row), move focus to the panel heading (`tabIndex=-1`). Keep the current behaviour for pointer opens. Add "Back to list" focus return on Escape (already wired through `onClose`).

title: Expanded disclosure contents aren't grouped, and switches drift from their labels
what: Privacy and terms: opening it reveals Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, Support and Delete my account as same-level rows. There's no indent or tint, and the summary loses its divider (`quiet.css:274`), so the children read as siblings. Each topic row is about 130px tall;. The switch drops to its own line, about 700px from its label;.
why: Gestalt common region and proximity; Fitts's law (the switch is far from its label).
fix: Put disclosure bodies in an inset block (the `q-disclose__body` treatment: 12px radius, `#F2F5F4` fill, 16px inset, `quiet.css:754`), or indent child rows 16px. Lay the switch row out as a two-column grid (`minmax(0,1fr) auto`, `align-items: center`, `min-height: 64px`).

title: "What changed in your schedule" list is unsorted and cramped
what: The rows read Wed, Sat, Mon, Sun, Tue, Thu, Fri. Hairlines sit directly under the second text line with no bottom padding. All seven rows say "Added" with no chip or icon, so a real removal or time change won't stand out.
why: Miller's law (chunk and order); visual hierarchy; similarity.
fix: Sort by shift date. Use 12px vertical padding per row. Use a status chip per change: green "Added", amber "Changed", grey "Removed" with words, per the B chip rules.

title: Start and End offer 96 quarter-hours from midnight
what: `timeChoices()` returns all 96 `QUARTERS` starting at 12:00 AM (`schedule-shift-form.tsx:28–31`). Reaching 9:00 AM in the desktop listbox is 36 steps, and the list has no default.
why: Hick's law; Fitts's law (scroll distance).
fix: Default Start to the location's usual opening time, or the previous shift's start, and End to Start plus 8h. Order the list so it opens scrolled to the default. Keep typeahead.

title: Off switches nearly vanish, and the switch is 31px tall
what: The off track is `--c-field #D5D8DA` on a white card: 1.43:1 (`corp/corp.css:186`), under a white knob. The switch is 51×31px (probe: `input.c-switch` ×36 and `input.q-tog` ×64 under 44). C6 covers field edges, not the switch.
why: WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (control boundary and state); Fitts's law.
fix: Off track `#8C9397` (3.12:1), or keep the light fill with a `1.5px #6A7176` inset ring. Give the switch a 44px hit area: `::before { inset: -7px -2px }`, or let the whole `label.c-shift__lead` row be the target (already a `<label>`, so make it at least 48px tall).

title: Colours are 1,345 literals across four slightly different token sets
what: The --b-* tokens are scoped to .b-screen, so the shell and desktop layers can't use them. Corp and Quiet keep their own ink, grey, line and canvas values, and Quiet's warm greys still show wherever B misses a rule.
why: A subtle "two apps" feel; every colour change needs hundreds of edits.
fix: Move --b-* to :root under [data-nv-b] and repoint --c-* and --q-* at it in one block. Replace literals file by file, starting with owner-b-desktop.css (280 literal uses).

title: Text sizes sprawl in half-pixel steps
what: Ten sizes sit between 12 and 17px (47 uses of 14.5px, 31 of 15.5px). Sheet titles use five sizes, empty-state titles two, line-heights mix px and unitless, and letter-spacing mixes px and em.
why: Steps 0.5px apart read as misalignment, not hierarchy.
fix: Define a role scale with paired line-heights: caption 12.5, meta 13.5, body-sm 14.5, body 15.5, title-sm 17, plus display sizes. One sheet-title size (20/26 700), one empty-state title (16/22 600), em-only tracking.

title: Cards, notes and buttons cast seven different shadows
what: At least seven recipes in three notations draw "the soft layered shadow", from four shadow base colours, and the teal primary has five glows. Notes sit in card stacks at radius 16 with their own shadow beside 22px cards.
why: Neighbouring surfaces show visibly different depth and hue.
fix: Define --b-elev-1 (card), --b-elev-2 (popover, sheet) and --b-elev-glow from one --b-shadow-rgb: 16 40 38. Give notes 22px and --b-elev-1, or no surface.

title: Disabled controls have nine different looks
what: Disabled states use opacity .45–.6, three grey fill and ink pairs and white-on-band variants, with cursor default ×14 and not-allowed ×4.
why: People can't learn what "not available yet" looks like.
fix: One pair: --b-disabled-bg #F0F2F3 and --b-disabled-ink #8C9397, no shadow, no scale, cursor not-allowed.

title: Retired styles and components still ship
what: employee-style.css (50 KB), signature/dark.css, auth-premium.css (23 KB) and 536 :not([data-nv-b-off]) selectors still load; AuthShell, passkey-slot branches, clocker-pin-icon and employee-shift-picker have no live caller.
why: Extra CSS on every load, and stale selectors that re-match if an attribute comes back.
fix: Drop the employee-style.css and dark.css imports from the app layout, delete the dead TSX and the :not([data-nv-b-off]) chains, and limit auth-premium.css to classes still rendered.

title: Owner and Employee desktop duplicate the shared layout and drift 1–2px
what: 37 identical declarations repeat across owner-b-desktop.css and employee-b-desktop.css, and 13 conflict (band button 48 vs 42px, live label 13 vs 13.5px, stack padding 24 vs 32px).
why: Each fix has to be made twice, and the two drift.
fix: Move the shared B-screen desktop layout into one block keyed on [data-nv-b] .b-screen and decide each of the 13 conflicts once.

title: Patch rounds append rules instead of editing them, and one selector is 3,050 characters
what: Many rules are set twice in the same file (owner-b-desktop max-width 1104 then 1152; corp has 21 such pairs). About 465 :has() uses and a 3,050-character selector mean one invalid branch drops a whole rule silently.
why: Reading the file gives the wrong value; the next fix edits a dead rule.
fix: Fold each pair into the original rule and split mega-selectors into one rule per page pattern.

title: Older stylesheets still load under Direction B
what: premium-clean-manager.css (226 KB), corp-shell.css, portal-premium.css and globals.css (374 KB) all load, and data-nv-clean is still set for Owner and Manager.
why: Every older rule B forgot is a latent mismatch.
fix: After cascade layers land, audit what B still relies on and stop setting data-nv-clean once B covers Owner and Manager.

title: Payroll details repeats its period line
what: "Oct 19–25 · Payday Fri, Oct 30" appears in the band sub-line and again as the card title right below it. "View" and a bare download glyph form two adjacent targets per document.
why: Redundancy; two targets for one document.
fix: Title the card "Totals". Give each document one trailing "Download" pill with a "View" link, or a 40px labelled icon button.

title: Card headers and group labels differ across sibling settings pages
what: Group labels sit outside cards on some pages and inside on others, and inner text starts at 117, 119 or 123px.
why: Consistency between sibling pages.
fix: Card titles inside cards with a teal-50 count pill ("Locations 2") on index pages, section labels outside on long forms, and one 22–23px inner inset.

title: Insights shows a nearly empty chart and pale placeholders
what: "Hours by day" draws a single bar labelled "87" on a 1,080px track with no baseline, the range reads "Nov 9 – 9 so far", and attendance dashes render at 2.29:1.
why: An empty chart reads as zeros.
fix: Write "Mon, Nov 9 so far". Hide the chart until two days have data, or draw future days as dashed outlines with a baseline. Show "—" in #6A7176 with "Not enough data yet".

title: Who's working lists only who is in
what: Four rows sit on an 812px card with a collapsed Time corrections accordion that doesn't belong there. Late or missing people, the reason to open this view, aren't listed.
why: The view should answer "who is missing?".
fix: Add "Scheduled, not in" rows with amber chips under the clocked-in group and move Time corrections to the Time area.

title: Small wording fixes across the app
what: Examples: "Open Past timecards" (case), "Tap a time" on desktop, "Updates every 30s", "Requesting recovery. Please wait.", "Checking setup..." with three dots, "Brand saved" on Branding, toast region named "Notifications", finder actions that don't echo button names, and "Remove" / "Keep" with no object.
why: Voice and consistency.
fix: Apply the copy audit's Low rows: sentence case, the … character, verb plus object on buttons, and labels that echo page and button names.

title: "Can't work" rows use a teal clock icon
what: A call-out is a wait-or-check event, but it gets the information tint (`inbox-b.tsx:105`, tone `teal` for `cant-work`).
fix: Use `tone="amber"` for `cant-work`.

title: This page uses a different row recipe
what: Rows have no leading tinted icon or face, unlike every row on Things to do. One title ends with a stray period ("Nov 2 – Nov 8."). The footer "Some attendance comparisons are unavailable." offers no action.
fix: Use `BRow` with the group icons used on Things to do, strip the period, and link the footer to Who's working.

title: "Recorded" repeats under every value
what: The caption is repeated 7 times, although the hero tile already says Recorded. The mock places the status there instead ("On track").
fix: Show the status (On track, Over, Ready to approve) under the value and drop "Recorded".

title: The timecard sheet uses its own type for times and a different note shape
what: The Days list sets AM and PM as small caps ("8:00 AM – 4:05 PM", `.c-ampm`). No other phone screen does. The "Needs attention" note has a 12px radius instead of 22, and its only bullet repeats the header status ("Correction awaiting review").
fix: Render AM and PM at full size with a U+202F narrow space, as everywhere else. Give the note 22px corners. Lead with the action ("Review Luis's correction before approving") rather than repeating the status.

title: Profile's phone number reads oddly spaced
what: "555-0100" renders with wide gaps ("555 - 0100") from the tabular figures plus Inter's wide hyphen. T4 notes the same hyphen problem.
fix: Exclude phone numbers from `tabular-nums`, or use a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011).

title: Setup gaps are grey text, and count headers come in three styles
what: Settings shows "Clocker tablets · 1 not set up" as grey text, and count headers come in three styles (plain, chip, count). Clocker tablet rows order location and status differently.
fix: Show "1 not set up" as an amber chip. Use one meta order (location · status). Use one header pattern, "Title + count chip", as on Home.

title: Small Settings inconsistencies
what: Features: the locked switches (Time off, Shift swaps) are "on" in pale teal, so it is ambiguous whether they are on. Branding: the preview's "Clock in on the Calle Loíza tablet" looks like a live teal button, with no "Preview" frame. Locations: "Northside Bakery — Conda…" is truncated in the list (the full name is one tap away).
fix: Draw locked-on switches in full teal with a lock glyph. Wrap the branding preview in a dashed "Preview" frame and make it `inert`. Allow two lines for location names.

title: Two submit patterns on sibling recovery pages
what: Recovery code and account deletion disable their submit until valid. Clocker recovery validates on submit. The disabled pills are near-invisible (`#F0F2F3` on the canvas) and give no reason.
why: Consistency; better-accessibility prefers validating on submit.
fix: Keep the buttons enabled and validate on submit with inline errors, as Add employee does. Keep the deliberate safety toggle on deletion.

title: The right rail wraps short descriptions and leaves the column empty
what: "Every request, waiting / and decided" and "Swaps and covers / between teammates" wrap at 353px. Below y≈470 the column is empty for 1,300px.
why: Use of wide space.
fix: Make the rail `position: sticky; top: 84px` so the shortcuts stay in reach while the list scrolls, and shorten the sub-lines to one line.

title: Closing the panel makes the page jump
what: The panel exits by moving up about 44px and fading, while the table widens from 988 to 1240 under it. The half-transparent panel overlaps "Approve 2 ready" and the Status column for the frame. A right-hand panel should leave to the right, or fade in place.
why: Exits are shorter and smaller (better-ui); layout stability.
fix: Fade the panel out over 150ms with a fixed `translateX(12px)`, and delay the table re-flow until the exit ends. Under reduced motion, use opacity only.

title: Panel header and anomalies
what: The header copies the iOS sheet: a centred "Timecard" title with a "Done" text button and no ×. Valeria Díaz's "113 h 19" in one week has no flag. "This week" folds no-time people into one row, while "Last week" lists "Jose Natal 0 min — No time yet" as a full row.
why: Jakob's law (desktop side panels: left title plus ×); anomaly salience; consistency.
fix: Left-align the title and add a 40px × button (keep Escape). Add an amber "Over 60 h" chip when recorded time is over the policy limit. Collapse no-time rows the same way on every tab.

title: Two navigations on Time exports and Payroll settings
what: A "‹ Payroll" back link sits above tabs that also contain "Payroll". The Payroll home has the tabs but no back link.
why: Navigation clarity; redundancy.
fix: Tab pages drop the back link, since the tabs are the navigation.

title: The empty state is centred in a left-aligned system
what: "This payroll isn't available" is centred with a grey button. The other empty states are left-aligned (Week templates, My pay, Clocker recovery).
why: Consistency; alignment to shared edges.
fix: Use the one empty-state pattern: a left-aligned icon in a tinted circle, a 16/22 600 title and the action as a pill. (Size T3 is covered in the code audit.)

title: The "Periods with no payroll" count pill differs
what: This pill is grey with a larger dark number, while every other count pill is teal-50 at 12.5px 700.
why: Chip consistency.
fix: Use the teal-50 pill, or a red-50 pill if the count means overdue.

title: The Clocker PIN back link is "Cancel" with no chevron
what: The Clocker PIN page's back link says "Cancel" with no chevron, while every other secondary page uses "‹ Parent".
why: Consistency.
fix: Use "‹ Maria Rivera".

title: Add employee: no back link and no stepper
what: "Step 1 of 2" is text only. Error text carries no icon (meaning sits in colour plus words; acceptable). The error state grows the card by about 56px, which is fine.
why: Wayfinding.
fix: Add "‹ Team" to the band and a two-dot step indicator. Optionally add a 14px `WarningCircle` to each error line.

title: Updates details
what: The tab count format "Needs reply · 1" differs from "Waiting 7" and "All 16". The update message card has 30px top and 45px bottom padding. "Withdraw update" is a full-width outlined pill on the canvas, which reads like a card.
why: Chip and tab consistency; spacing rhythm.
fix: Use "Needs reply 1". Equalise the padding at 22px. Merge "Read by" into the message card's footer, and make Withdraw a red text button in that footer.

title: Profile rows
what: Phone has no chevron while Email has one, and the reason is not stated.
fix: Add a lock icon or a chevron consistently, with OD-029's read-only pattern.

title: Settings polish
what: Features shows only a thin check on the selected row with no radio affordance. "1 not set up" is grey though it is a check state, the Branding preview button has 8px corners, and footnotes start at three different x positions.
fix: Use radio circles on single-choice lists, an amber chip for "not set up", the real pill in the Branding preview, and align footnotes to the card's 22px inner edge.

title: Availability is a dead-end list
what: "Not sent 1 / Sent 9" sits on the canvas (OD-077). Miguel Reyes's row has no action ("Remind") and no chevron.
fix: Add a quiet "Remind" pill, and move the segment to the band.

title: "Nov 2 – Nov 8." trailing period; the same period appears twice
what: Two separate rows read "Nov 2 – Nov 8." and "Nov 2 – Nov 8", with no visible reason for the split (it's likely by location).
fix: Drop the period and add the split reason ("· Calle Loíza" / "· Condado").

title: Desktop link card loses the icons and sub-lines the phone has
what: On desktop, Timecards' "Time exports" and "Time corrections" links are bare rows, while the phone shows the same links with icons and sub-lines.
fix: Use the same row with icon and sub-line at both widths.

title: Payroll wording on a page Managers reach while Payroll is denied
what: "Who's included and sent files · People in this payroll and where files went" and "File format · Columns your payroll provider needs" next to a Payroll page the Manager is refused.
fix: For roles without payroll, use "Export history · Files you've downloaded".

title: Add shift and Add employee: inconsistent field placeholders, and a 36px Save
what: Add shift says "Choose" while Add employee says "Choose one" and leaves name fields blank. The Save and Next pill is 67×36.
fix: One placeholder word ("Choose"). Give the header pill a 44px hit area via `::after`.

title: The phone's selected filter chip is solid black
what: The chip is black (`#111517`), the only black-filled control in the product. Selected states elsewhere are a white thumb on glass or teal-50 with teal text.
fix: Selected chip in teal-50 `#E8F3F1` with teal `#0B6E69` text and count.

title: The Hours this week stepper is a white pill straddling the band
what: Schedule and Activity use a glass stepper on the band. This one is a white pill on the band's edge.
fix: Use the glass stepper (DESIGN.MD:1417).

title: Request list polish
what: Approved rows have no chevron and no green "Approved" chip. The detail page repeats "Maria Rivera" in the band sub-line and the card header. Relative times read "5 min ago" on Time off but "6 min" on Shift requests.
fix: Use a green chip and a chevron. Drop the band sub-line on the detail page. Use one relative-time format with "ago".

title: Help: inline links are 19–20px tall; Delete account's back link points to a page that doesn't link to it
what: Help's inline links (Forgot access, Account recovery, the support email) are 19–20px tall. Delete account's back link says "Profile", but Profile has no delete row; the way in is Help › Account deletion.
fix: Pad the inline links to a 44px line box, or turn them into rows. Set the back link to the referrer ("‹ Help").

title: Help someone sign in: the ID example doesn't match real IDs
what: The Employee ID placeholder says "e.g. 10482" while real IDs look like "QA-SCAN-A" or "OWN-ELENA".
fix: Use an example in the workspace's ID format.

title: Earlier notifications show their date twice and have no chevron
what: "Action needed · Thu, Nov 5 · 2:41 PM" sits beside a right-side "Nov 5", and the rows are links with no chevron.
why: Redundancy and row affordance.
fix: Keep the date on the right, put only the time in the sub-line, and add the chevron.

title: The finder shortcut label swaps after load and shows on touch tablets
what: The search trigger renders "⌘K" on the server and switches to "Ctrl K" after hydration, and "Ctrl K" shows on touch tablets that have no keyboard.
why: Stability after first paint; don't show keyboard hints on touch.
fix: Render the hint empty on the server and fill it on mount, and hide it under (pointer: coarse).

title: The "not published" note floats on the canvas away from the schedule
what: The note saying next week isn't published sits on the canvas between cards instead of inside the schedule card it qualifies.
why: Proximity and common region.
fix: Move the note into the week card's header or footer.

title: Sideways phones still show the old corporate layout
what: At 844×390 the Employee Home shows the corporate page, not Direction B. DESIGN round 4 accepted this, so the reviewer did not log it as a defect.
why: Tablets and desktop are now Direction B, so landscape phones are the last surface on the old look.
fix: Decide whether landscape phones get the Direction B phone layout or the tablet layout.

decision.q: Sideways phones (844×390) still show the corporate page, as accepted in round 4. Revisit now?
options: Give landscape phones the Direction B phone layout.
Keep the accepted corporate layout for now.
decision.rec: Revisit after the High fixes; it is the last pre-B surface people can reach.

title: "Open shifts · None right now" is a link to an empty page
what: A full row with a chevron leads to "No open shifts right now".
why: Information scent; Hick's law.
fix: When the count is 0, render it as a static row without a chevron, or fold it into a line under the week card: "No open shifts · Get alerts".

title: The time zone exists only for screen readers
what: The probe found ", Puerto Rico time" as `b-sr` text in the hero sub. Sighted users see times with no zone, while Updates detail shows "AST".
why: Consistency; equal information.
fix: Either show the zone where it matters (people who work in several zones), or drop it from both.

title: Small inconsistencies inside the Fix my time form
what: The Start and End fields have no clock icon; time-off's time fields do (employee-state-requests-new-part-day-390…png). The selected radio row's teal outline has square corners against the group's 22px radius. The Day select defaults to "Sat, Oct 10", a month back.
why: Similarity; nested radius.
fix: Use one time-field component. Give the selected row's outline the inner radius on first and last rows (`border-radius: inherit` on the first and last child). Default Day to empty, matching "Choose a day" in the incomplete state.

title: Desktop Pay cards end at different heights
what: On desktop Pay, the "Last paycheck" and "Earlier" cards end at different heights (y=438 and y=429).
why: Edge alignment.
fix: Use `align-items: stretch` on the two-column row.

title: The desktop "Shift requests" card's second row says one thing and does another
what: "My schedule — Start a swap or cover offer" goes to Schedule. The phone has no such card, so Requests has no route to Pick up and swap on phones.
why: Information scent; parity.
fix: Title the row "Swap or give away a shift" (the copy audit's wording). Show the same two rows on phones under Decided.

title: The "Waiting" chip repeats on every row of the Waiting tab
what: On the Waiting tab every row repeats the amber "Waiting" chip, which the tab already says.
why: Redundant information.
fix: Hide the chip when the tab already filters by that status, or show the part-of-day or duration in its place.

title: Count format on tabs differs by width and page
what: Tab counts read "For you · 1" on desktop, "For you" with no count on phone, and "Unread 9" on Notifications.
why: Similarity.
fix: Use one format: the label plus a small count pill, at every width.

title: `/app/exchange/swap` without a shift silently shows Open shifts
what: Opening /app/exchange/swap without choosing a shift silently shows Open shifts with no explanation.
why: Visibility of system status.
fix: Show a note card first: "Choose the shift you want to swap" with "Open Schedule".

title: The same disclosure has two titles
what: The same disclosure is titled "Shifts you can't pick up 1" on Schedule and "Why other shifts aren't available" on Pick up and swap.
why: Consistency.
fix: Use one title, and show the count in both.

title: The same action has two names, and the detail's H1 is generic
what: The update list says "Confirm" and the detail says "Acknowledge update" for the same action, and the detail's H1 is the generic "Team update" with the real title second.
why: Consistency (the copy audit owns the wording); hierarchy.
fix: Use one verb. Make the update's own title the H1, with "Team update · Management · Nov 9, 9:25 PM" as the sub.

title: Small Profile details
what: The language segment is 34px tall. The Profile error shows "–" for Name while the account menu on the same screen shows "Maria Rivera".
fix: Extend the hit area to 44px. Fill Name from the session the shell already has.

title: Help's Contact card mixes a link row with a dense policy paragraph
what: Five lines of 13.5px grey sit under the email row, with a bold warning at the end.
why: Hierarchy; density.
fix: Keep one line ("We reply within two business days"). Move the warning into a tinted note with the lock icon. The full hours text can live on Support.

title: List dividers switch between inset and full-bleed inside one card
what: A second `<ul class="b-list eb-desk">` at `home-b.tsx:220`. `waitingExtra` outside the list at `requests-b.tsx:107`.
why: Similarity; continuity.
fix: Render those rows inside the same `BList`, or give `.b-list + .b-list` the inset top border that rows use.

title: Desktop focus order zig-zags between the columns
what: DOM order is shift → team → to-dos → upcoming. On screen that is left, right, left, right. Tab goes from "Shift details" (x 611, y 570) up to the team row (792, 379), then back down to Things to do.
why: WCAG 2.4.3, focus order. It is still understandable, so this is a recommendation.
fix: With LN-005's column wrapper, the DOM can follow the columns: the left column (shift, to-dos), then the right (team, upcoming).

title: Repeated markers and repeated totals
what: Seven identical "Shift lead" chips appear when every shift is a lead shift, so the marker no longer distinguishes anything. The desktop week card footer repeats the band sub-line "7 shifts · 59.5 h".
why: Redundancy and signal-to-noise.
fix: When every shift in the week is led, show one line in the card header ("You lead all 7 shifts") and keep only the today block's chip. Drop "7 shifts · 59.5 h ·" from the footer. The first change needs Jose's sign-off, because the chip is specified per block.

decision.q: When a Lead leads every shift, seven identical "Shift lead" chips appear. The chip is specified per block. Collapse it?
options: One header line ("You lead all 7 shifts") and the chip only on today's block.
Keep a chip on every block.
decision.rec: Collapse to one line when every shift is led.

title: For you and the deep links don't match Open shifts
what: Open shifts has a titled card ("You can pick up 2"). For you is a bare row-card with a 3px left accent and no card title. `/app/exchange/swap` and `/app/exchange/callout` render the tab lists (page titles "Open shifts" and "My shift requests"), not a swap or can't-work form. The manifest records "no visible submit". A deep link lands on a generic list.
fix: Give For you a card header ("Needs your answer"). Have /swap and /callout without a shift either redirect to Schedule with a hint ("Choose a shift to swap") or open the shift picker.

title: Mixed alignment at the foot of the card
what: On desktop the disabled "Save" pill is right-aligned while "One-off days off go in Requests." is centred under it. "One-off" renders with a wide hyphen ("One - off"), a new instance of T4. The card body starts at x 315 while the header starts at 319 (see LN-050).
fix: Left-align both, or make Save full width as on phone with the hint centred under it, and apply T4's `font-variant-numeric: normal` to text.

title: Update rows and update detail polish
what: At 390, "Management · Mon, Nov 9 / · Unread" starts a line with "·", which breaks the Dotted rule. In detail on desktop, card 1's text is at x 315 and card 2's at 319 (LN-050). The list button "Confirm" becomes "Acknowledge update" on the detail page for the same action.
fix: Render that meta with `Dotted` (`messages-b.tsx:172`). Use one verb ("Confirm") on both.

title: Profile and browser Alerts details
what: "Security" holds only "Delete my account" in this configuration (no passkeys row). The English/Español segment is 77×34 on phone (probe), below the 48px Direction B target. The desktop Alerts row puts its icon at x 315 and text at 363, against 319 and 377 for every other icon row.
fix: Retitle the section "Account" when it holds only deletion. Give the segment a 44px hit area (`account.css:121`). Use the standard `b-row` geometry for the Alerts row.

title: Owner More duplicates the rail on a tablet
what: Insights, Updates and Settings are rail items; More repeats them, and no rail item lights while it is open. Sign out is left-aligned red text here but centred on the Employee More (`T/employee-more-900.jpg`).
fix: From 768, keep More reachable only from the account menu, with the rail state on Home. Centre Sign out in both, or left-align it in both (C13 covers the red).

title: "Clock in on the Main Office tablet" looks like a button
what: It is a filled grey block with an icon in a tinted circle, the shape of a tappable row, but it is informational.
why: False affordance.
fix: Use a plain inline note (icon plus text with no fill), or make it link to "Where's my tablet?".

title: "Get alerts on this phone" on a tablet
what: Tablets see "Get alerts on this phone".
fix: "Get alerts on this device".

title: Availability belongs to Requests on phones but to Schedule on tablets
what: The phone tab map puts `/app/availability` under Requests (`src/lib/navigation.ts:246`).
why: Consistency across devices (Jakob's law).
fix: Pick one home for Availability and apply it to both maps.

title: Setup card alignment and duplicate status
what: 1. The "Setup code" label is left-aligned, but the hint under the field is centred: `.hint` has no `text-align` and inherits the card's centre (clocker.module.css:207). The field gets two left edges. 2. The lead wraps so a line starts with the arrow: "→ Clocker tablets." This happens at 1024 and 768.
why: Gestalt continuity and common alignment edges; Hick's law.
fix: Add `.hint { text-align: left }`. Bind the path with a no-break space before the arrow (`Settings → Clocker tablets`), or wrap it in `white-space: nowrap`. Keep only the button's busy label and drop the `.busy` line on the setup form.

title: The status chip and the detail line repeat each other, and the 66px indent creates a third left edge
what: `.strow` and `.breakContext` are indented 66px (:257, :265) to sit under the name. The note, the message and the action rows start at 0. At 1024 that gives three left edges in one card (avatar 492, chip 558, note 492). At 390 it forces "under a minute ago" onto its own line. The detail repeats the chip's word.
why: Shared alignment edges; Miller's law (redundant tokens add load).
fix: Drop the indent at ≤599px: `@media (max-width: 599px) { .strow, .breakContext { margin-left: 0 } }`. Make the detail time-only: "Since 10:43 PM · under a minute ago". The label at `clocker-punch-panel.tsx:202` would become "Since"; the copy owner signs off.

title: The "kept for review" message after Review has no icon and starts on a different edge
what: The teal `.msg` (`clocker-punch-panel.tsx:193`, css :161) starts at x=492 with no icon. The detail line above starts at 558. Every other `.msg` carries an 18px icon.
why: Consistency between states; Gestalt continuity.
fix: Render the notice with `<ClockerIcon name="info" size={18}/>`, as in the PIN error. Give the ready-screen notice the `.note` box, which the no-break-types notice already uses.

title: The initial's face tint can land on red or pink, beside a red = stop vocabulary
what: `faceTint` (`src/lib/face-tint.ts:4`) produces a red family for "James". On a kiosk where red means stop, the first thing shown beside "Hi, James." is a red-tinted circle.
why: One colour, one meaning (the tint is decorative, but it lands in the status hue).
fix: On the Clocker, exclude hues within 15° of `--ck-red` (and of amber) from the face palette. Alternatively, use the teal soft tint for every face on the kiosk.

title: "Help with a saved action" adds a choice at decision points
what: `handoff(false)` renders on every non-ready mode (`clocker-punch-panel.tsx:256`).
