Choosing a break type or confirming Clock Out therefore carries a third, unrelated teal link, about the tablet's other saved records, under the two real choices. On Clock Out? it sits where a hurried thumb ends up after "Cancel clock-out".
why: Hick's law; Fitts's law (an extra target near the decision).
fix: Exclude `select-break` and `confirm-out` from line 256: `!['select-break','confirm-out'].includes(mode)`. It stays on Ready and on the recovery states, where it's relevant.

title: The receipt states the time three times, and its 13.5px line ends on an orphan
what: The time appears in the band clock (10:43), the hero ("10:43 PM") and "Saved at Nov 9 · 10:43 PM". The hero is approved. The "Saved at" line wraps to leave "seconds." alone at 1024 (`.saved`, :302).
why: Miller's law (redundant tokens); better-typography `text-wrap: pretty`.
fix: Add `text-wrap: pretty` to `.saved` (:302). Show the date part only when it differs from today, which is how `shortTime()` already works at :34.

title: Under reduced motion, frozen bars read as progress
what: Under reduce, `.progress > i` is frozen at `translateX(80%)` (clocker.module.css:334). A 38%-wide block parked at the right reads as "80% done", a determinate bar that never moves. `.countdown > i` loses its animation and stays full for the whole 8s (:331), saying "full time left" until the screen vanishes.
why: Better-ui "every animated state change leaves a static cue that is true".
fix: Under reduce, hide the progress fill (`.progress > i { display: none }`) and keep the track plus the "Keep this screen open…" text, or show a static full-width track at 40% opacity. For the countdown, step it with a non-motion change: `ckClear` with `steps(8)`. A discrete width change is not motion, so it is acceptable under reduce.

title: Single-exit states have no primary, and the storage error uses the "refresh" glyph
what: "Return to PIN" is the only way forward, but it renders as a grey secondary (`clocker-punch-panel.tsx:192`), so the screen has no clear next step. Browser Storage Needed uses the amber `refresh` ring (:183), the same as "Check Your Last Action", though nothing can be refreshed there.
why: "fill exactly one action per view"; icon meaning.
fix: When `leave` is the only button (modes `auth` and `storage`), use `data-kind="primary"`. Use `warning` (WarningCircle) for `storage`.

title: The photo flow uses a third disclosure style and mixes alignment
what: "View photo notice" and "Get help" use the browser's default ▶ marker (`photo-notice.tsx:11,17`; no `list-style: none`). Elsewhere the kiosk uses a trailing Phosphor caret ("Action reference ⌄", "Help with a saved action ⌄"). The description is left-aligned under a centred ring and heading.
why: One icon family per surface (better-ui); shared alignment edges.
fix: Add `.flow.flow .photoNotice summary { list-style: none; display: flex; justify-content: space-between }` plus `::-webkit-details-marker { display: none }`. Add a trailing `<ClockerIcon name="caret" size={16}/>` that rotates when open, as `.reference` does (clocker.module.css:308–310). Centre `.flow.flow .description` to match the card.

title: The teal band defeats automated contrast checks
what: The probe and axe measure band text against the canvas or white behind the border-image band, reporting 1.05–1.10:1 for every band title. Real failures on the band hide among hundreds of false ones.
why: Automated checks can't guard the band until it is painted as a real background.
fix: Paint the band as a background-color plus gradient on the hero element (not border-image), so axe and the probe read the true pair. Then re-run the audit to catch real band failures.

title: Puerto Rico Spanish: "tiempo libre" means leisure, "Importe" is Spain usage
what: Time off is translated "tiempo libre", which reads as leisure in Puerto Rico; payroll documents use "Importe". "Patrono" is already right.
why: Terms should sound local and mean paid leave.
fix: Choose "días libres" or "licencia" for time off and "Cantidad" or "Monto" for amount, then add them to the glossary.

decision.q: Which Spanish word should NEVORA use for paid time off?
options: "Días libres" (solicitud de días libres): plain and common.
"Licencia": more formal, closer to HR usage.
decision.rec: "Días libres" for the UI, matching the glossary; keep "licencia" for formal documents if needed.

title: The desktop card is unevenly padded and jumps when an error appears
what: On Sign in there are about 76px from the card top to the "Good evening" cap height, but 32px from the links to the card bottom. On Forgot it's about 70px above the back link and 44px below the last link.
why: Proximity and balance.
fix: Find and remove the empty top box so the card padding is 32/32. Use `align-self:start; margin-top:clamp(64px, 16vh, 160px)`. The card top then stays fixed and the error only pushes content down.

title: The brand panel outweighs the form and breaks to three lines in Spanish
what: The panel line is 48px/700 white, heavier than the card's 34px title. The first fixation lands on the marketing line, not the form. The mock says "The form is the first thing you can touch". "NEVORA Workforce" above it repeats the wordmark. At 1024 ES the line breaks "Tu semana, / en un solo / lugar.", which defeats `TwoLines` (auth-shell.tsx:135).
why: Figure-ground and visual hierarchy; Spanish line breaks.
fix: `font-size:clamp(36px, 3.4vw, 46px)` on `.q-auth__line`, and `white-space:nowrap` on each `TwoLines` span from 1024px. Optionally drop the eyebrow, since the wordmark already names the product.

title: At 320 in Spanish, the secondary pill and the help disclosure wrap
what: "Tengo un código de / recuperación" wraps inside a 52px pill. "¿Dónde encuentro mi ID de / empleado?" wraps with the chevron hanging on the first line.
why: Translation growth; Fitts's law (an irregular target shape).
fix: `text-wrap:balance` on `.q-btn` and on `.ma-details summary`. The copy audit already proposes shorter Spanish.

title: The phone's rule checklist looks like radio buttons
what: The unmet rules use hollow `CircleIcon` at 18px in grey, which reads as selectable radios.
why: Gestalt similarity with form controls.
fix: Unmet: `Circle` with a dashed stroke, or `MinusCircle` bold in `#6A7176`. Met: `CheckCircle` bold in green `#1D6B45` (green = done). Keep the list `aria-live="polite"`.

title: On phones the wordmark jumps from left (Welcome, Help) to centre (forms)
what: Mobile-access.css:146–149 apply the centred three-column header only `:has(.ma-card)`.
why: Gestalt continuity across one flow, Welcome to Sign in.
fix: Drop the `:has(.ma-card)` condition so every Mobile Access header uses the grid.

title: The title leaves a single word on its second line
what: Headings such as "Brighter work / ahead." and "Tu día empieza / aquí." leave one word on the second line because of a 13ch cap (mobile-access.css:72).
why: Typography (balanced headings).
fix: Remove the 13ch cap and set `text-wrap:balance` on `.q-hd h1`.

title: The footer crowds the help card, and "Need help?" points at the page you're on
what: "Need help?" sits about 11px below the card at 1440 and overlaps it visually at 1024. Other auth pages keep about 100px. On `/access-help` that link goes to `/access-help`.
fix: Hide `.ma-footer-help` on the help routes (auth-shell.tsx:144). Keep a margin of at least 28px between `.q-auth__col` and the footer.

title: The 404 is English-only, and its "Error 404" line is under AA
what: An ES visitor gets an English 404 with no language switch. "Error 404" is white at 0.78 alpha on the band: about 4.4:1 at 15px (not-found.css:33). This is a new instance of the design audit's C1.
fix: Read `readAuthLang()` and use `AUTH_COPY` strings. Set the eyebrow alpha to at least 0.86. Clocker hint: not captured, because the 404 shots use `/no-such-page`, not `/clocker/…`. From the code (not-found-hint.tsx:9, not-found.css:37), the hint is an amber note, `#6E3C00` on `#FDF3E4` (8.28:1, passes). That fits "amber = check". It has no icon; the mock draws one, so add a `DeviceTablet` bold icon.

title: Footers wrap one item onto its own line
what: At 320 in Spanish the footer wraps "… Términos ·" then "Ayuda" alone, and policy footers split "Account / deletion".
why: Spanish and translation line breaks; Gestalt proximity (the separator is stranded at the line end).
fix: Wrap each link with its leading " · " in `<span style="white-space:nowrap">` (brand-legal.tsx:26–27; legal-document.tsx:105–107). Or render the links as a flex list with `gap` and CSS `::before` separators.

title: Back links and secondary links are styled differently on every page
what: Three back glyphs and labels, and teal links at weights 400 and 600 and at 15 and 17px.
why: Similarity; Jakob's law.
fix: Use one back control everywhere: Phosphor `CaretLeft` bold 16px, label "Sign in", weight 600, 15px. On desktop auth pages make it the white pill at the top left, as in mock 7. Set all teal text links to 600 / 15px.

title: The error's position differs between Sign in and Recovery
what: Sign in shows its error at the top of the form, while Recovery and Reset show theirs below the submit button (code read; the state wasn't captured).
why: Consistency; proximity to the cause.
fix: Move the recovery and reset alerts above the fields. The focus-on-error logic already exists.

title: Revoked: the destructive button sits between two neutral ones
what: The order is Check again (quiet), Turn off alerts (red outline), Review app setup (quiet). There is no primary, and the red button sits in the middle of the thumb zone.
fix: Check again (teal), Review app setup (quiet), Turn off alerts (red outline) last.

decision.q: Revoked alerts list Check again, Turn off alerts (red), Review app setup, with no primary. DESIGN lists this order. Reorder?
options: Check again (teal), Review app setup (quiet), Turn off alerts (red outline) last.
Keep DESIGN's order.
decision.rec: Reorder so the destructive action is last and one action is primary.

title: The wordmark appears twice
what: A white "NEVORA" in the band, then a grey "NEVORA / Workforce" lockup with the coloured "A" under the card (`unsupported-role.tsx:14,22`).
fix: Keep the band wordmark and reduce the footer to "Powered by VELANI LLC".

title: The finder surface still wears the pre-B kit
what: Radius 14px;. A 1px border;. A neutral `rgb(28 28 28/.22)` shadow;.
why: Consistency, similarity.
fix: Under `[data-nv-b]`, give `.command-finder` a 22px radius, no border and the shared popover elevation (`--b-elev-2`, per S2). Use the B scrim colour on `::backdrop`.

title: Small finder details
what: The SSR text is `⌘K` and an effect rewrites it (`command-finder.tsx:138,166`). The hint visibly swaps on Windows and Linux. The Employee and Lead placeholder is "Search your pages" while the dialog's name is "Find a page, person or place" (`:111` vs `:168`).
why: Stability (no content swap after first paint); 2.5.3 Label in Name spirit.
fix: Render the hint empty server-side and fill it on mount, or set it from the user agent in the server component. Pass the role-specific label to `aria-label`.

decision.q: The Employee and Lead finder (Ctrl K) has no Actions. DESIGN marks this "default until Jose decides". Add them?
options: Add Request time off, Swap a shift and Set availability as finder actions.
Keep the finder to pages only for Employees and Leads.
decision.rec: Add the three actions; they are the most common employee tasks.

title: ActionMenu naming details
what: `aria-label` on a role-less popover `div` (`action-menu.tsx:161`) is ignored, since ARIA naming is prohibited on generic elements. `title={ariaLabel}` on the trigger (`:138`) adds a native tooltip ("Jose Natal, account menu") that repeats the name. The trigger and menu icons are regular weight; see I1, not repeated.
why: WCAG 4.1.2; noise.
fix: Give the non-sheet popover `role="group"` (or drop the label) and remove `title`.

title: The Person field shows an empty avatar circle
what: `c-av c-av--grey` renders an empty grey disc before a person is chosen (`schedule-shift-form.tsx:111`). It reads as a broken image.
why: Aesthetic-usability.
fix: Render a UserIcon bold 16px in the tinted circle until a person is chosen.

title: The entrance blurs the page title, not just the cards
what: The b-enter stagger is applied to the hero text as well as the cards. The page's identity (its h1) is unreadable for the first 300–600ms of every arrival. Whether it also runs on routine tab taps, which DESIGN 1386 forbids ("No motion on routine taps"), was not verified.
why: Better-ui "stagger infrequent entrances"; Doherty (orientation first).
fix: Keep the hero static and stagger only `.b-stack > *`. Run the entrance on first load per session, not on every tab change.

title: The leave-repair note uses its own amber and green
what: The repair note's 4px amber edge is #D98A1B (2.76:1) and its green #1F7A45, different from the chip tokens.
why: Non-text contrast and one amber.
fix: Use #8A4B00 at 4px (or the amber-50 fill with an amber ring) and #1D6B45.

title: Band extensions are painted with shadows, outlines and border-images
what: Phone pages extend the band with box-shadow 0 -14px 0, a 14px outline and a border-image.
why: Fragile: a focus ring, forced colours or a changed band colour shows seams.
fix: Paint the band once on the page container, as desktop does.

title: Reduced-motion fallbacks differ slightly between surfaces
what: Under reduced motion the phone sheet appears instantly while desktop cross-fades; one entrance has no fade fallback; the b-enter keyframes live inside a media query other files depend on.
why: Consistent reduced-motion behaviour and no hidden dependency.
fix: Use the 160ms opacity cross-fade on the phone sheet too, add the b-fade fallback in requests.css, and move @keyframes b-enter and b-fade to top level.
